During the war, Prince Demchugdongrub's army also conquered and annexed the province of Suyiuan, fighting alongside the Japanese Army. It ceased to exist in 1945 when it was invaded by the Soviet Red Army and Mongol Red Army as part of the Manchurian Strategic Offensive Operation. Most of the area is now a part of the People's Republic of China.

During the war, the threats faced by tanks have multiplied, from enemy tanks, anti-tank guns, dedicated tank destroyers, all the way to modern infantry weapons firing shaped charges that can penetrate even heavy armor. We must develop new protection methods to keep our own tanks alive in the face of these threats.

During their prototyping phase, special projects go through multiple prototypes before they are completed. The outcomes of these prototypes can vary depending on the project, the category of project, and previous choices made in the special project. Each outcome has a weighted random chance of firing, though some outcomes can only fire when the project has more than some amount of progress and/or less than some (other) amount of progress.

During this period, do the focuses in your political tree for all of the crazy army buffs, but also grab Suomen Maavoimat. Don't bother with the economy tree focuses; there's no point. They were designed with a small Finland in mind, not one that had 100 factories in 1937. When World Tension hits 25%, immediately start prioritizing the Extra Refresher Exercises branch. Every focus in that section is quite strong, particularly Salvaged and Retooled. Both support companies offered there are quite good too.

Taking Allow Trade of Special Goods and Promote Paper Bank Notes is not required, but the buffs are nice. After that go down the right side of the focus tree, pick Instill Three Rules of Discipline and continue until Cooperate with Ulanhu Have one factory on artillery and the rest on guns. Later on add trains, Anti-Air and Trucks (but only when you can produce a good amount of guns and arty on a steady base).
During World War I, there was an invasion by the Russian Empire ( ⟦0⟧) who were supported by the ⟦1⟧ as well as by their old rivals the Ottomans ( ⟦2⟧) who were supported by the ⟦3⟧.

During World War II, between 1940 and 1941, several cities in the region would be attacked with bombing raids by ⟦0⟧. The British in 1942 also fearing that Erwin Rommel would be victorious in seizing Egypt or that Germany would invade from Syria which was controlled by ⟦1⟧, began to build a series defensive lines and fortifications in northern Palestine. In addition to this during 1943 Germany would start a propaganda campaign in the region to try and convince Palestinians Arabs to revolt against the British. This not only was not successful in then end but in fact several thousand Palestinians would volunteer for service in the British Army during the war.

During World War II, British India fielded the largest volunteer army in the war, and used it to contain the Japanese advance into Burma, as well as stopping Japanese advances into the Indian subcontinent. The Battle of Imphal was a critical victory that stopped the ⟦0⟧ army's advances from occupied Burma. The war, however, was not without consequences to the people of the Raj, as wartime needs for the military often superseded any civilian concerns. A massive famine in the Bengal region was blamed upon the limited food aid sent by the British in favor of sending those supplies to the European and African theaters.

During World War II, continental Norway was invaded and occupied by Germany in spring 1940. The four-man team on Jan Mayen stayed at their posts and in an act of defiance began sending their weather reports to the United Kingdom instead of Norway. The British codenamed Jan Mayen 'Island X' and attempted to reinforce it with troops to counteract any German attack.

During World War II, Iceland joined Denmark in asserting neutrality. After the German occupation of Denmark on 9 April 1940, the Althing replaced the King with a regent and declared that the Icelandic government would take control of its own defence and foreign affairs. A month later, British armed forces conducted Operation Fork, the invasion and occupation of the country, violating Icelandic neutrality. In 1941, the Government of Iceland, friendly to Britain, invited the then-neutral United States to take over its defence so that Britain could use its troops elsewhere.

During World War II, in 1941, Nazi Germany, Fascist Italy, Hungary, and Bulgaria occupied Yugoslavia, redrawing their borders to include former parts of the Yugoslavian state. A new Nazi puppet state, the Independent State of Croatia (NDH), was created. With the Treaties of Rome, the NDH agreed to cede to Italy Dalmatian territory, creating the Governatorate of Dalmatia, from north of Zadar to south of Split, with inland areas, plus nearly all the Adriatic islands and Gorski Kotar. Italy then annexed these territories, while all the remainder of southern Croatia, including the entire coast, were placed under Italian occupation. Italy also appointed an Italian, Prince Aimone, Duke of Aosta, as king of Croatia.

During World War II, the Belgian Congo served as a crucial source of income for the Belgian government in exile in London after the occupation of Belgium by the Nazis. Following the occupation of Belgium by the Germans in May 1940, the Belgian Congo declared itself loyal to the Belgian government in exile in London. The Belgian Congo and the rest of the Free Belgian forces supported the war on the Allied side in the Battle of Britain with 28 pilots in the RAF (squadron 349) and in the Royal South African Air Force (350 Squadron) and in Africa. The Force Publique again participated in the Allied campaigns in Africa. Belgian Congolese forces (with Belgian officers) notably fought against the Italian colonial army in Italian East Africa, and were victorious in Asosa, Bortaï and in the Siege of Saïo under Major-general Auguste-Eduard Gilliaert during the second East African campaign of 1940–1941. On 3 July 1941, the Italian forces (under General Pietro Gazzera) surrendered when they were cut off by the Force Publique. A Congolese unit also served in the Far Eastern Theatre with the British army in the Burma campaign.

During World War II, Yugoslavia sought to remain neutral in the conflict. However, the Italian invasion of ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ cut Yugoslavia off from any form of non-Axis support. Eventually, Yugoslavia bowed to the pressure from its neighbors and joined the Axis on March 25th, 1941. In response to that deal, a number of anti-German military officers staged a successful coup against the royal government and declared the treaty of entry to the Axis to be void. This greatly angered the German, Italian, and Hungarian governments, all three of which simultaneously invaded on April 6th, 1941 in a response of their own. Within 10 days the Yugoslavian forces surrendered. This rapid defeat was caused by both the poor state of the Royal Army and of the refusal of the Croat population to defend the hated Serb-dominated government. Much of Yugoslavia's territory was annexed by the three invading powers, as well by the Axis-allied ⟦2⟧. The remaining portion of the country was divided into two satellite states, a Croatian state led by the fascist organization ⟦3⟧, and a Serbian state under German 'protection'.

Dynamic intel pool can be manipulated through the following defines: FLAT_DECAY and MULT_DECAY control the rate at which the intel decays The formula is applied as follow (runs daily): NextIntel = ( Intel - FLAT_DECAY ) * MULT_DECAY AGGREGAT_LOG_FACTOR and AGGREGAT_DIVISOR control the rate at which intel accumulates. It is applied to the sum of the intel generated throughout the day as follow: Aggregat = LOG_FACTOR * log( 1 + IntelOfTheDay ) + IntelOfTheDay / DIVISOR The Aggregat is then added to the pool of intel. If DIVISOR is zero then the division is evaluated to zero. MAXIMUMS controls the maximum value that the pool can contribute to the final intel values. ABSOLUTE_MAXIMUMS defines a ceiling for the intel in the pool that will never be exceeded. They are meant to be greater or equal to MAXIMUMS. If the array is empty, no absolute maximum is defined. E.g. a 36 width division with 1000 attacks has five 14 width divisions with 200 defense on its list of targets. There are no additional modifiers to coordination in play. 650 attacks will then be allocated to the split attack. Each enemy division will receive 130 of those. The remaining 350 that was partitioned off with then be applied to whichever is considered the best target. If there are no other divisions left to be assigning attacks, the attacks are then compared to defences and resolved as hits. The 4 sub-targets will each receive 130 attacks compared to their 200 defense, while the primary target will receive 480 compared to 200 defense. If there was a second attacking division that had the exact same distribution, the sub-targets would each receive 260 hits against 200 defense, and the primary would get 960 against 200 defense.

Each balance of power consists of 2 or more sides. While a balance of power can contain more than 2 sides, at any time the player may only see 2 which are chosen in the effect to initialise the balance of power. A side having power only has a cosmetic impact, changing the icon and the text used in scripted localisation. A side isn't inherently set as being left or right, instead it is assigned which side is on which half when the power balance is initialised.

It is possible that they may prove useful in the role of occupation or garrison troops, despite their lack of apparent combat capability. Mobile units are capable of outpacing infantry units and are a valuable asset for an army. Each country has a special forces cap that dictates the maximum amount of special forces battalions they are allowed to field. This cap is the greater of either 24⟦0⟧ battalions or 5%⟦1⟧ of the total amount of non-SF battalions making up the rest of your deployed divisions. Divisions cannot be changed, trained, given a different template or have their template adjusted if that would result in exceeding the SF cap. By default, to increase the SF cap beyond the default 24 without any bonuses, you would have to exceed the 480 non-SF battalion breakeven point by 20 for each additional SF battalion. For example, you would need 500 non-SF battalions for 25 SF battalions, 520 non-SF battalions for 26 SF battalions, 540 non-SF battalions for 27 SF battalions, etc. These battalions do not need to be fully equipped or be at full strength, they just need to be part of divisions that are deployed in the field.

Each Faction Theater requires a Theater Commander. A country that owns a Faction Theater may assign any of its Field Marshals or Admirals as the Theater Commander. The Theater Commander will only give bonuses to divisions controlled by the countries selected, within the regions it has been assigned. The Theater Commander's country receives a portion of the Mastery earned by other faction members in the theater based on the commander's Attack and Defense skills. Each special project category has a number of potential special projects that can be pursued. Special projects have a breakthrough cost that must be paid to start them and go through three phases. The first, establishing phase happens every time a special project is started or restarted. The second, initial research phase only needs to happen one per special project, and if a project is stopped in the middle of this phase, progress is retained for if/when the project is restarted. The third, prototyping phase is the longest phase and involves the creation of successive prototypes that build progress until the phase has reached 100% completion. The amount of time it takes to develop each prototype depends on the special project, and the amount of progress each prototype produces both depends on the special project and is also somewhat random. When a prototype is finished, it can also produce one of many possible ⟦0⟧, some of which can add or remove progress, produce an assortment of effects, and/or prompt the player to make a decision about how to proceed with the project. When the prototyping phase is complete, the special project in question is complete.

El Salvador had a fascist dictatorship ruled by Maximiliano Hernandez Martínez since 1931 which repressed minorities in his country such as Chinese, Indian and black peoples among other groups. In 1932 there was a revolt done by indigenous peoples that were culturally repressed. The uprising failed and that group would continue suffering even more over time. El Salvador was neutral during the first world war. In the 1936 Olympic games, El Salvador didn't compete because the Olympic team wasn't recognized by the committee of the Olympic games until 1938. In the 1938 football (or soccer) world cup, El Salvador didn't participate. Before the United States of America entered the second world war, El Salvador was improving relations with all the fascist countries in the world. Soon after the American declaration of war on the Axis powers, El Salvador has joined the Allies. El Salvador has sent money and equipment to the Allied powers, also supplying the USA with manpower on a promise of American citizenship should they survive. Salvadoran troops have supported American troops during the D-day landings. At the time, El Salvador based its economy around farming, primarily in the elements of coffee, sugar, and corn.

Even though Paraguay is a landlocked nation with almost no industry, manpower or resources, Paraguay has a neighbor called ⟦0⟧ that is in a very similar position. However because Paraguay is a communist country it can justify wars right from the beginning in 1936. What this strategy consists of is to justify a war as soon as you can against Bolivia. Once you have your war goal ready, you will stay in a defensive position on the border with Bolivia because the Bolivian AI will endlessly attack your line. After a period of time the Bolivians will have lost most of its manpower and equipment attacking your line and they won't be able to break through. When you see that the Bolivians are low on equipment then you can start to push and invade their lands without too many problems. Again though the key is to be entrenched and let their army grind away on your front line until their troops are weakened. Once this happens only then should you put your army on the offensive. It may be worthwhile to consider building land forts and infrastructure on the border before the war to make things easier on your army when the Bolivian AI starts to grind away on you. Then when you capitulate them, you will just annex them. After this you can attack other countries (the best option would probably be ⟦1⟧). Be warned though no matter which other neighbour you attack next, it will be more difficult. Chile has among the strongest infantry division templates in South America at the very start of the game, and being only a few tiles wide you may have to deal a long war as you take the country one tile at a time as you make your down to the capital. In essence Chile will do the same thing to you as what you want to do with the Bolivians. Alternatively you could try to attack Peru or Argentina however both have larger armies and more manpower meaning in order to win you need finish the war as quickly as possible before they can produce more divisions. It is probably worth producing paratroopers for these options as you can land forces behind their lines to either pull forces off their front or conversely to pin down forces so they can't reinforce divisions your frontline army can defeat. It is strongly advisable to not attempt to attack Brazil unless you have conquered at least two other neighbouring nations to gain more manpower and factories. Another option is to join the Second World War by joining one of the factions, however if you do this while tensions are high and you are attempting to conquer one of your neighbours it will likely result in the other nation joining an opposing faction. The most obvious faction to join would be the Soviet Union in the Comintern as you already are communist and can join at any point. Or the Axis if you go fascist though this means one would have to switch ideologies. Even though you can join in on the side of the Allies, this would probably result in much less territorial expansion.

Expeditionary Force divisions can gain experience but their template may not be modified by the receiving country. Players receiving Expeditionary Forces may wish to provide Lend-Lease shipments to the home country of equipment types that it may use to supply the Expeditionary Forces.

Expeditionary Forces get their equipment and manpower from their home country, not the recipient. The recipient has full control of them until returned. War score for occupation by an Expeditionary Force goes to the country controlling them, while war score for casualties goes to the home country (the one providing the Expeditionary Force). Their ongoing supply however is supplied by the controlling country, this means you can use expeditionaries to offload supply pressure if their supply situation is better than yours. Since the other Chinese states usually do not make or field any armor or much artillery, this means that a tank-using Manchukuo can gain a considerable combat advantage over their units. By researching the 1934 and 1936 Light hulls and using cheap modules such as the One-Man Turret, Small Cannons or Automatic Cannons, Diesel or Gasoline engines, Riveted Armor and Bogie Suspension, one can keep the tanks cheap while allowing for them to be functional and useful. Alternatively, by using a Light Fixed Superstructure as the turret, one can make use of Medium cannons and Howitzers, which are much more effective against infantry, but ineffective against armored, motorized or mechanized units. To provide support for the tanks without losing too much speed, add ⟦4⟧ into the armored division, or, if resources/fuel supplies don't allow that, then use ⟦5⟧ units as a stopgap instead. If tanks are to be Manchukuo's main weapon of choice, then one should choose the Mobile Warfare Land doctrine and select the Embrace the Future and Motorization Drive ⟦6⟧ spirits to help with swiftly creating and integrating armored units into the army.

First nation to deal with is Peru. In every scenario Peru, has finished its war against Ecuador, and exhaustion might have worn them out a little. Regardless, the first 3 focuses one should take are ⟦0⟧ ⟦1⟧, and ⟦2⟧ - for the political power you get, either hire Mikhail Kalinin or take Improved Worker Conditions for a much needed stability boost (note that until Bukharin is in charge, you will not be able to earn much political power - although you can somewhat offset this by infiltrating the civilian governments of other countries; if playing on ahistorical, there's a chance Turkey might back down when you mobilize the armed forces in response to them remilitarizing the Bosporus, thus giving you some stability and political power). After that, take ⟦3⟧ and ⟦4⟧, then go up to Partial Mobilization, and round it off with ⟦5⟧ - while you might think that ⟦6⟧ is a good idea if not working with the Left Opposition, doing so will boost Paranoia, so it's best avoided. Second, do not build any factories in the 11 states that will form the Confederacy - the states in question were the same ones that revolted in the original American Civil War (the Carolinas, Mississippi, Florida, Alabama, Georgia, Louisiana, Texas, Virginia, Arkansas, and Tennessee). While building a few factories there is fine for the missions to get congressional support for the focuses that require it, focus the majority of your development in the North.

First, one should strengthen the civilian government, and prepare for a civil war. You'll lose your most highly skilled generals but keep Admiral Yamamoto. Your forces will be split, so disband your army, take Army Expansion Law, and use 5 of the army XP you get to create a unit with a single artillery division, then train as many as possible (divert the majority of your military factories to produce artillery), and when the war begins, deploy the ones you kept and convert them to infantry/cavalry (because of how frail this template is, it'll fall relatively easy - a single untrained cavalry unit alone can defeat a stack of 24 of these units). If you wish to get into one additional war aside from the ones against Manchukuo and Germany, justify a war goal on Siam before the civil war fires - you'll keep on justifying after flipping to democracy, and of the nations you can attack, Siam is the only one that has no difficulties (Nepal, Tibet, and Bhutan don't have anywhere you can attack from, Mongolia is allied with the Soviets, the Raj, Indies, Australia, New Zealand, and Malaya are attached to the Allies, and you can't attack China/any of the warlords) - Purge the Militarists before you justify, since the more time you have to prepare, the better.

First, one should wait until they have enough political power to justify on ⟦0⟧; while the country itself (and ⟦1⟧, who is one of the 3 nations guaranteeing Yugoslavia) is not required to form the HRE, it is guaranteed by 2 nations (France and Czechoslovakia) who are. In the meantime, use your starting infantry to guard the border with France, convert all your starting units who aren't infantry to the Panzer Division, and have them prepare a naval invasion from Wilhelmshaven to either Dunkerque or Calais. Train and force deploy cavalry until you have 48 units, and use them to guard the Czech border - make sure to exercise them so they aren't lv 1. Have your navy exercise until they are at least lv 2, and then set them on strike force on the necessary bodies of water. Your focuses should be Naval Rearmament, Army Innovations, Treaty with the USSR, Air Innovations, Four Year Plan, and Großraumwirtschaft - use the 10 Army XP you get from Army Innovations to add 2 motorized units to your Panzer Division Template, to make them faster and stronger, and use the bonuses from Four Year Plan to go ahead of time on the 1939 Industrial and Construction techs. Note that while Align Romania would allow you to eventually bring Romania into your faction (thus allowing you to get around the Romanian guarantee of Yugoslavia), by the time Romania would be able to join your faction, France will have joined the Allies as well as having cancelled its guarantee on Yugoslavia, so it's best to just hold off on aligning Romania (and it's best to wait until after you overthrow the Nazi regime to get them as a puppet anyways).

First, start to position your divisions so you can impose martial law on the Dominions once you flip Fascist. You need to place divisions in your dominion's states so your have enough manpower to impose martial law. The minimum manpower requirements are:

First, take the Focus Never Another Gallipoli. While that is going, arrange your meager divisons into a small army. Begin your construction by building Infrastructure in Central Australia as well as anywhere that there is 1 Level or less of Infrastructure. Begin improving relations with other Pacific countries like Japan, the Dutch East Indies, and the United States. Start your research by researching Carriers, Basic Machine Tools, and Construction I. After you finish Never Another Gallipoli, take the next focus, Protect the Homeland. By this time, the first round of Infrastructure should be finished and you should start by building a mixture of Infrastructure and Civilian Factories in your provinces. Once Construction I and Basic Machine Tools are finished, research Distributed Industry and Excavation I. Protect the Homeland should be finished by now, so choose Sever Ties With UK as your next focus (ignore The SWPA Menace for now).

Firstly, take the "Western Focus" and "Reinforce Old Alliances" then I would suggest the "Axis Investments" but "Attract Allied Capital" would be fine. You have two options after this, either wait until world tension builds up and justify against Hungary and or Bulgaria and turn them into puppets, while completing the "Limited Self Governance" and "A United Autonomous Croatia". Feel free to do the Industry Branch in the meantime if time allows. Otherwise, you can ignore this step and to continue onwards and just complete the two focuses. After this you need to take focuses that allow all of your territories autonomy, then do the Industry Branch. Take "End the Regency" as soon time allows after these focuses, as you will be able to have Peter II to grow up sooner than else. Take all three reunification focuses of the "A United Kingdom" sub branch, as you will gain cores over all your subjects, including Transylvania (Autonomous Region of Transylvania), Hungary and Bulgaria (If you puppeted them earlier. Albania, Romania and Greece do not get cored, however, so don't bother). This effectively allows you to become the most powerful country in the Balkans, as you have a core manpower of over 24 million and should have over 30 Civilian Factories and quite a few military factories. With this power, you can stop a German or Italian attack head on. Feel free to consider turning into a democracy later on.

Firstly, take the first three focuses on the Communist Branch. After that, the 4th focus requires 40% communist support, which will take time. Depending if the player picked "Form Peasants Council" before or after "Soviet Economic Aid", has or hasn't used Anti-Communist raids (decisions) or a Communist Revolutionary in the government, the difference of these modifiers may take from 2 focuses up to 4 focuses before you can pick "Abolish the Monarchy". While waiting to reach the 40% requirement, use the national focus in the meantime to expand the Yugoslavian manpower and industry. After completing "Abolish the Monarchy", take "Yugoslavian path to Communism" in adherence to Titoism. Then, the player should logically take "Form the Federal Republic" in order to remove all the negative spirits.

Flags are added in for cosmetic tags the same way as they would be added for the base appearance of countries: three 32-bit TGA-file flags with no RLE encoding with the bottom-left origin point are added into ⟦0⟧ and its subfolders and their usage is based off the filename.

Flags can also be targeted towards a certain country. This is usually done by appending the ⟦0⟧ to the name of the flag, though it can be placed anywhere within the tag name except for the first character. For example, ⟦1⟧ will set it to be targeted towards the country represented by PREV, which we'll take as TAG. ⟦2⟧. After this, ⟦3⟧ will come up as true for the same country it was set in. This can be used to create dynamic flags without relying on ⟦4⟧. You cannot have more than one target specifier in a single tag, You can only use @ROOT, @PREV, @FROM, and @THIS, even @PREV.PREV does not work. Both of these restrictions do not apply to targeted variables, so those may be a more flexible alternative if you need.

Flags used for countries in ⟦0⟧ and its subfolders.

Flags within PDXScript are a 32-bit signed integer, ranging from -2147483648 to 2147483647. A flag can only be set to a specific value (Potentially for a certain amount of days), modified in an additive way by a certain value and read, no other operations can be done. ⟦0⟧ serve as a more operational alternative, with far more capacity for changing (Such as multiplication or non-integer values, reading game values, being able to set to other database entries rather than numbers, etc). Flags are still recommended to use as a boolean value, as these are more optimised than the variables, and so using variables will lead to an unnecessary increase in memory usage and will lead to the game running slower compared to flags.

Following ⟦0⟧’s victory in the Second Italo-Ethiopian War, the territories of ⟦1⟧, Eritrea, and Italian Somaliland were unified into ⟦2⟧ in May 1936. Following is a history of changes to the constants:

Following Lenin’s death in 1924, Joseph Stalin gradually consolidated power, outmaneuvering rivals within the party. By the early 1930s, the ⟦0⟧ had embarked on a program of rapid industrialization and forced collectivization of agriculture, transforming the nation’s economic base at the cost of widespread famine, suffering, and political repression. The Great Purge of 1936–1938 further tightened Stalin’s grip, eliminating perceived enemies within the military, party, and intelligentsia, but leaving the Red Army weakened on the eve of global conflict.

Following the 1842 defeat of the British-Indian forces and victory of the Afghans, the British established diplomatic relations with the Afghan government and withdrew all forces from the country. They returned during the Second Anglo-Afghan War in the late 1870s for about two years to assist Abdur Rahman Khan defeat Ayub Khan. The United Kingdom began to exercise a great deal of influence after this and even controlled the state's foreign policy.

Following the Anschluss of Austria in March 1938 and the Munich Agreement in September of that same year, Adolf Hitler annexed the Sudetenland from Czechoslovakia on 1 October, giving Germany control of the extensive Czechoslovak border fortifications in this area. The incorporation of the Sudetenland into Germany left the rest of Czechoslovakia with a largely indefensible northwestern border. Also a Polish-majority borderland region of Trans-Olza which was annexed by Czechoslovakia in 1919, was occupied and annexed by Poland following the two-decade long territorial dispute. Finally the First Vienna Award gave to Hungary the southern territories of Slovakia and Carpathian Ruthenia, mostly inhabited by Hungarians.

Following the armistice with the Allies, Marshal Pietro Badoglio’s royal government saw much of Italy swiftly occupied by Germany. In the north, the Germans installed Mussolini as head of the puppet Italian Social Republic, based in the town of Salò between Milan and Venice. Badoglio and the king fled to Brindisi in the south without issuing orders to the army. The royal government, controlling southern Italy, declared war on Germany and claimed authority over the entire nation, sparking a brief but destructive civil war marked by partisan resistance. By spring 1945, with the war's end, Italy lost Istria and the city of Zadar to Yugoslavia, as well as all its African colonies. In the postwar years, Italy recovered and became a founding member of the European Union alongside ⟦0⟧, Germany (then divided into West Germany and ⟦1⟧), and the Low Countries.

Following the capitulation of Poland, it is advisable to maintain a defensive position against Germany until the United States enters the war. Given that the Soviet Union is to receive half of Poland, this leaves two potential frontlines against Germany. The first objective can be achieved by maintaining a defensive position at Königsberg, where there is a three-province border, or by initiating a strategic withdrawal along the five provinces adjacent to the Nemunas River (six provinces, if Wilno is secured following the capitulation of Poland). Should one possess a well-balanced military force, including a means of penetrating the enemy's lines and a robust assault capability to counter German tanks, particularly in the later stages of the conflict, then a strategy of holding one's position while fortifying it could prove an effective approach.
Following the death of Tsar Boris III, his father Ferdinand I will sit on the throne once again, seeking revenge against those who wronged him decades ago.

Following the fall of ⟦0⟧ in June 1940, Romania had to come to terms with German supremacy on the continent. In July 1940 the ⟦1⟧ demanded that Romania cede northern Bukovina and Bessarabia, Romania accepted. In August 1940 Germany demanded that Romania cede northern Transylvania to ⟦2⟧ and in September southern Dobruja to ⟦3⟧, Romania accepted again. One-third of Romania's 1939 area was amputated in 1940 and with it Romania's population shrank from 19.9 million to 13.3 million, half of the lost population being ethnically Romanian.

Following the Nationalist victory in the Spanish Civil War against ⟦0⟧, Francisco Franco instituted a full dictatorship and suppressed the Republican partisans known as the Maquis.

Following the Second Boer War (1899–1902), South Africa was incorporated into the British Empire, becoming a self-governing dominion in 1910 as the Union of South Africa. Governed by a white minority, the Union implemented policies that entrenched racial segregation, such as the 1913 Natives Land Act, which restricted land ownership for Black South Africans. In 1931, the Statute of Westminster granted South Africa full legislative independence, enabling it to make its own decisions within the framework of the British Commonwealth. However, tensions persisted between pro-British factions and Afrikaner nationalists, many of whom sought greater autonomy from Britain.

Following the Spanish-American war of 1898, ⟦0⟧ was not annexed by the ⟦1⟧ in the Treaty of Paris unlike the other Spanish possessions of the Philippines or Puerto Rico. Instead it gained independence as a sovereign state due to the Teller Amendment passed by the US Congress that same year. Nonetheless, the American occupiers stayed until independence was granted in 1902. ⟦2⟧ remained heavily influenced by the ⟦3⟧, tariffs were cut, and the economy became dominated by their northern neighbor - 4 years after the war American companies owned 80% of Cuban ore exports along with most of the sugar and tobacco factories. Moreover, the ⟦4⟧ introduced the Platt Amendment which allowed the US army to intervene in Cuba.

Following the war, Malaya and Singapore returned to the British, this time with increased autonomy. After the return of the British, there were growing nationalist sentiment amongst the local populace, as many felt that the British were no longer competent in their administration and defence of the crown colony and its inhabitants. It became independent in 1957 and merged with Singapore, British North Borneo and Sarawak to form Malaysia in 1963. Singapore was expelled from Malaysia in 1965 and became its own sovereign nation.

For a large decrease, the game checks if the faction level is more than the variable ⟦0⟧ which is 9 points. If it is below 9 points, it only loses 5 points. If it is above 9 points, for each tier above Subdued, the game checks if the faction's points are above a certain number. If it is not above, it then gets demoted if it is not above a certain point limit. The values required for a decrease in tiers is as follows: Dominating to Influential requires 49 points, Influential to Meddling requires 34 points, Meddling to Subdued requires 19 points. It then loses 10 points.

For a large increase, the game does a similar check as the small increase, however the points required to increase tiers are different. Subdued to Meddling will automatically go up, Meddling to Influential requires 15 points, Influential to Dominating requires 30 points. It will then gain 10 points. Similarly, if there is a faction that is already Dominating, it will then be demoted to Influential and will be set to 35 points.

For the Axis, you can re-enforce Italy or Vichy France's soldiers in Syria and allow them to focus their manpower elsewhere by securing Syria and knocking out British forces in Kuwait (When taking Kuwait, you will have to leave 1-2 small divisions in Basrah, and Kuwait as British commonwealth forces will try to naval invade). When fighting in this front you can tie up many British and free French forces in Syria and the Levant region, keeping them from more important campaigns in Europe and straining their supplies in the region. Eventually you can make your way down to Egypt and take the Suez Canal, further assisting Axis forces. But on the other hand, with the allies you can take off pressure on the allies in the region by quickly expelling Vichy forces from Syria and protect the region from Italian infantry that will occasionally enter through Lebanon or the Sinai. Whichever option you choose, you must remain aware of your limited industry, supply lines, and the superiority of foreign forces as you fight in World War 2.

For the Commonwealth, Habsburg, or Romanian monarch paths, it is relatively simple. Rush down the focus that allows you to start making the monarch decisions in the country you want. I suggest saving political power 1 or 2 focuses before that focus, as you will need around 350 political power in total in making the decisions without spending any of your industrial power. Try to limit yourself to using the 50 political power decision for the first few, and then when the 25 command power and 25 political power decision becomes available use that in conjunction with the 50 political power. If it seems Germany or the Soviets may be annexing it earlier than expected, you can use the other decisions to quicken up the pace. If you get the politcal power needed and do the focus, the AI sometimes tries to counter this by using decisions that allow them to decrease monarch support thus canceling your focus. It can then be recommended to do monarchy support while doing your focus, even if it is somewhat wasted. Annex them as quick as possible.

For the Communist sub-branch, after the civil war, Japan may choose a leader, and depending on the leader, will then follow one of two paths. The leftmost path installs the Lecture Group, who gets their influence from Marxist-Leninist ideology. They focus on building industry in urban regions and establish a five year plan to build that industry. The rightmost path installs the Labor-Farmer Faction into power which focuses on investing in rural regions, reform the economy and unlocks the War Communism economy law.

For the Cossack or Romanov paths, just rush down the focus that allows you to annex land. I believe improving relations does help the country saying yes to your demands, so do that when you start the focus to demand something.

For the first step, in forming the super Kingdom of Franco-Spain, you must put on non-historical focuses, and restart saves until ⟦0⟧ does its focus Estado Novo. Once you get the news article detailing that there has been a royal marriage between ⟦1⟧ and ⟦2⟧ you can move on. Next step is forming the European Union. Follow the Forming the European Union steps for how to form it, but make sure to not go down any focus tree other than the monarchist branch, as well as making sure that the Carlists win the Spanish civil war and the monarchist Portuguese win their civil war and the Brazilian monarchist civil war (If they Don't fire, don't worry, that just means you don't have to help them through the ⟦3⟧). Note that you can still form the Kingdom of Franco-Spain if Carlist Spain did not win, provided that they did spawn (as you can liberate Spain to them in the peace deal), although doing so will lock you out of gaining cores on any Portuguese states.

For the first two above given options how the player chooses to expand will be influenced by who you border which will not always be completely predicable. However, there are several things which will always be the same and which must be carefully managed in order to expand. Jordan has only one province which means you start out with a tiny or non-existent industrial base, and a very small population. It is strongly advisable that one flips either communist or Fascist to take advantage of their respective options to boost manpower. Additionally changing your politics will allow you to join a larger faction such as the Axis or Comintern which will be needed if you wish to take any nearby British or French territories.

For the focuses, rush the right side of the political focus tree and aim for Request Control of The Railways. Before unpausing, disband all of the cavalry plus 1 infantry division and have the rest train indefinitely to get some ⟦0⟧. Research trains because you do not start with it, and be sure to research Paratroopers, Support Equipment, Light Tanks, Fighters, and if possible CAS. Build 3 ⟦1⟧ and the fill the rest with ⟦2⟧. Once the first focus is complete, spend the bad guns you start with on destroying the bandits which will get you 30 ⟦3⟧, then wait until your army training give you more until you have 35 ⟦4⟧ which should be spent immediately on State Serves the Military spirit on the Officers Corps, and you can stop the military training if the divisions are already at level 3. Once you finished researching trains, you should gain control of some of your own ⟦5⟧ and put 1 factory on guns, 1 on trains, 1 on transport planes, 1 on artillery, 1 on support, and adjust them as needed. Switch the transport planes to Fighters and then CAS once you got about 3 of them. Once you reach Request Control of The Railways, you can take the redirect tools 2 times and try to get just 1 military high command, you need the ⟦6⟧ and Command power later. Try getting your third research slot for now, plus Invite Japanese Settlers for more ⟦7⟧, then you want to focus on taking all of the focuses at the bottom before Independence War. You will want to take the right side (Five Equal Peoples) as it gives better bonuses and the way you are going to acquire your equipment later. You want to get to Purge the Generals Affairs Council first as you can increase your conscription law for cheaper before taking the rest.

For the vast majority of folders, such as ⟦0⟧ files, the ASCII character IDs are used to sort them by filename for the interpretation. This is different from the alphabetic sorting used by the file explorer as uppercase letters are considered to come before lowercase letters and there are multiple characters inbetween (such as underscores) that lie inbetween. In order to place a file particularly high in the evaluation order, a prefix using late character IDs such as ⟦1⟧ can be used and a reverse for the other way around, with the base game commonly using ⟦2⟧ for this.

For your military, France's 18-width 'Division d'Infanterie' is good, though support anti-air is a good addition. The mountaineers and motorized infantry are also useful, but everything else can be converted to regular infantry. Medium tank divisions can be useful for encirclements but the limited military industry means you can't build more than a few armored divisions. A railway gun can be helpful for defending on the Belgian border and pushing back into Germany. Finally, building a lot of 1936 fighters is the only real counter to Germany's huge air force. The naval game isn't especially relevant as Germany is unable to construct a substantial surface fleet and Britain is capable of subduing the Regia Marina in the Mediterranean. As far as strategy goes, let your enemies attack without counterattacking, then push only when your troops are at full strength while your enemies are down to 75% or so.

France boasts a somewhat modern - if badly understrength - fleet. Whilst the Marine Nationale is strong enough to decisively defeat either the Kriegsmarine or the ⟦0⟧ alone, it would have no chance against a combined Axis fleet. As with her tanks, France begins the game with modern naval technology, such as 1936 BB, DD and SS techs and two unique designs: La Fantasque, a destroyer model with tier 3 (1940) engines, and the Surcouf Class cruiser submarine. Many of these designs are clearly aimed against an anti-surface role, prioritizing fast, lightly-armored ships with minimal ASW capability and strong scouting capabilities. From 1.12 onwards, anything defined in ⟦0⟧ can be freely tokenized, even if defined in a totally custom enumeration block, seperate from the ones hard-coded into the game. It is therefore theoretically possible to define arbitrary tokens of a custom enum type in this file. However, for compatibility reasons, using ⟦1⟧ for custom enumeration types should be avoided, as this will ensure that the mod will not be compatible with any other mod that overwrites that file, no matter which mod gets priority on the file. As before, it's preferable to have a custom idea category with a set of dummy ideas in their own file that will not be overridden by other mods representing the values the custom enum can take on. This pattern is a useful replacement for passing around arbitrary integers that have some enumerable meaning when interpreted by code, especially if those integers are interpreted to yield names in scripted localisation, in which case this pattern can substantially remove the need for scripted localisation boilerplate by allowing defining the localised name for each enum member directly in a localisation file, as similarly to defining the localised name for an idea.

From 1941 to 1944, Greece would be occupied mainly by German forces, constantly under harassment by the Greek Resistance, one of the most successful resistance movements of the war. In October 1944, German troops finally withdrew from the country as the ⟦0⟧ invaded the Balkans, in an effort to avoid being cut off. By the end of the war, Greece was devastated. From an XP perspective, however, each soldier is worth more XP in a smaller division. So, it can be worth adding them to a small number of elite divisions. These could be things like marine or paratroop divisions, etc. Another possibility might be a regular infantry division that has already gained a high experience level on its own. By creating a duplicate template, a field hospital can be added to some divisions but not to otherwise identical ones, to help those high XP divisions keep their XP. The higher a division's XP gets, the more the average will be reduced by casualties (since replacements are always green). Deploying new divisions that have a field hospital while they are still green is a complete waste from the XP perspective. Therefore, you have more incentive to train new divisions up to regular before deployment when using field hospitals.

From the late 17th century, the Omani Sultanate was a powerful empire, vying with Portugal and Britain for influence in the Persian Gulf and Indian Ocean. From the manpower, war support, and HP perspectives, bigger is better. Each field hospital, being percentage-based, will simply save more lives and equipment in a large division than in a small one. This applies doubly so for helicopter med-evacs, as their bonus recovery rate is also percentage-based, and their fuel usage relative to the entire division goes down as the number of fuel-using battalions in the division increases.

From the start of the game go down the communist side of the tree and choose to "Compromise with the NKP". Delete your starting army and airplanes as with the previous strategy mentioned above. Conserve your political power until you reach "The Seeds of Revolution" and spend it all on the decisions it unlocks. The focus "Organize Partisan Militias" will allow you reach level 3 of the Revolution Decisions and spawns a couple divisions in the states you maxed. If done correctly you should be able to launch the civil war end 1936 and be communist soon after. After that build up your industry (both communist tree and economy tree give a good amount of factories). Justify on Denmark and annex them completely in the Peace Deal. Continue building your army and economy and have a justification for Poland ready for August / early September 1939. When Germany declares war you do the same, a couple in-game hours later Germany allows you to join the Axis. Together Defeat Poland/Benelux/France and then naval invade the UK. In the Peace Deal take Bourgogne and take England and try to get the states in East-Canada that border the USA. After that focus on spending the remainder of your points on the British Fleet.

Given the above points, it is viable to use extremely cheap destroyers (⟦0⟧) for convoy escort duty. Such destroyers lack sonar and depth charge equipment and are thereby not particularly well suited for anti-submarine warfare, but convoy raiding submarines will flee from them regardless. Given the lack of early industry and large fielded manpower requirements for many focuses, Romania will be fielding an almost exclusively infantry-based army for the first four years of the game. The beginning template of 9 infantry divisions should not be changed. All cavalry divisions on the field at the start should be converted to infantry. 20 new divisions must be queued up for training, and they should be given high equipment priority. The fielded divisions should be organized into two armies under an army group led by marshal Ion Antonescu. The whole army group should be placed at the Hungarian border and given an offensive line order. When it comes to doctrine, whatever the player chooses should be fine, but Superior Firepower would be the best choice for the early and mid-game and thus make the biggest difference. As concerns airpower, the two fighter squadrons should be combined into one. They will be used to support the coming invasions, but will not make much of an impact. The air force will be given proper attention later. When it comes to naval forces, Romania's starting fleet is laughable. Thankfully, naval power is not needed until much later - the fleet can stay safely in port at Constanta for the next 5-6 years, during which submarines and destroyers should be built for it with the available shipyards.

Given the limited initial manpower and industry of Chile, if facing bigger opponents like Argentina or Peru, one possible strategy is to go for a more defensive approach by employing ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧. Take advantage of terrain features like rivers as well as any terrain that inflicts a penalty to attacking units, like mountains, hills etc., to maximize the effect of your fortifications. A strong and properly built defensive line (especially if built in layers of multiple successive fort lines) can allow the player to more easily hold off attacks by stronger opponents and inflict casualties to drain their manpower and equipment. When the enemy army is suffering from attrition and exhaustion launch a decisive counterattack to cut off the enemy's supply lines and maybe even encircle and destroy some of their units. One example includes building a defensive line through mountainous terrains and using it to hold off Peru to buy time, allowing Chile to build ⟦2⟧, allowing it to then deploy ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧ or even Tank units to launch a counterattack and score a breakthrough.

Glorious though it may be, the path to victory for Puyi, and by extension Manchukuo, is littered with challenges and hardships to overcome in order to prove his right to the throne. The first of these, which Manchukuo has to deal with right from the start, is the problem with Banditry. As long as this problem persists, outlaws, criminals and communist partisans will periodically launch raids against state property, causing damage to factories, infrastructure and the like, posing a major problem in that Manchukuo's starting industrial base is already very limited. Taking the national focus ⟦0⟧ will unlock a set of decisions that allows Manchukuo to either hunt down or pacify the bandits. If Manchukuo elects to pacify the bandits, they will have to station enough units in the chosen province and maintain control there for 180 days to neutralize the bandits, which is slower than the alternative but unlocks a set of decisions to recruit the bandits into the army afterward. If Manchukuo, on the other hand, decides to hunt down the bandits, then they just need to take the decision (which will cost 500 Infantry Equipment and 1000 Manpower), removing the bandits instantly but preventing you from recruiting them later.

Götterdämmerung introduced the Assault Engineer Company and Armored Engineer Company as a variants of the engineer support company. They are made available after completing the Military Engineering Vehicles special project, though the Armored Engineer Company also requires having completed the 1938 Armored Engineer Company technology. These use armored support vehicle equipment in place of some support equipment and infantry equipment. The equipment differences mean they have increased production cost and add fuel usage to the division, increase its supply use, and reduce its Defense, but they can also provide some additional Armor, Piercing, Soft Attack, Hard Attack, and Breakthrough to the division depending on the equipment variant(s) used. Assault engineers trade most of the engineers' terrain defense and movement bonuses for terrain attack bonuses, and they also provide significant attack and movement bonuses in urban terrain. Instead of providing additional entrenchment to leg infantry battalions, they provide addition breakthrough to those battalions. Armored engineers lose defense bonuses in jungle, marsh, and river terrain compared to regular engineers, but give greater movement bonuses in more terrain types, and provide additional attack bonuses in rivers, forts, and urban terrain as well as in amphibious environments (naval invasions). Armored engineers also provide additional Breakthrough to armor battalions. Tech upgrades to engineers also provide these two support companies with similar bonuses, with assault engineers receiving greater attack bonuses but no defense bonuses and armored engineers receiving greater defense bonuses but no attack bonuses. Due to these differences, assault engineers are best used in offensive divisions, while armored engineers are more niche and best used for defensive divisions that are meant to guard key provinces important enough to justify the increased production costs, especially urban provinces.

Götterdämmerung introduced the Helicopter Brigade support company, which is unlocked by completing the Helicopters special project. Where other helicopter support companies like helicopter recon, helicopter med-evac, and helicopter tranports are specialized alternatives to non-helicopter-based support companies, the helicopter brigade functions as something standalone that can be added to a division regardless of what other support companies it is using. On top of the extra Armor, Piercing, Defense, and Breakthrough that the company provides from its use of helicopter equipment, the helicopter brigade provides a mix of bonuses that the other three, more specialized companies would give: extra Reconnaissance, reduced Supply Use, extra manpower trickleback, extra war support protection, reduced XP loss from taking losses, and extra HP for infantry, motorized, and mechanized battalions. These bonuses, however, are only upgraded by the 1942 technology upgrades for recon companies, logistics companies, and field hospitals, which can make fully upgrading helicopter brigades more difficult compared to one of the specialized helicopter support companies. Unlike the more specialized companies though, helicopter brigades neither add fuel usage nor increase existing fuel usage.

Helicopter Med-Evac is a variant of the field hospital company made available after completing the 1938 Helicopter Med-Evac Company technology that requires having completed the Helicopters special project. It requires helicopter equipment in place of some truck equipment. The equipment differences mean it has increased production cost and adds fuel usage to any division it is added to, but it also provides some additional Armor, Piercing, Defense, and Breakthrough to the division. Compared to field hospitals, helicopter med-evacs have greater supply use and provide less XP loss reduction and bonus HP, but they provide greater manpower trickleback and war support protection and provide additional Recovery Rate to all infantry, motorized, and mechanized battalions. Upgrading helicoptier med-evacs provides smaller bonuses to XP loss reduction compared to upgrading field hospitals, but instead provices greater bonuses to manpower trickleback, war support protection, and bonus Recovery Rate.
Helicopter MIO traits Tandem and Single Rotor are now in the right columns

Helicopter Transports are a variant of the logistics company made available after completing the 1938 Helicopter Transport Company technology that requires having completed the Helicopters special project. It requires additional helicopter equipment in addition to the normal equipment required by a logistics company. This means it has increased production cost, but it also provides some additional Armor, Piercing, Defense, and Breakthrough to the division. Unlike other helicopter support company variants, it does not add fuel usage to a division that does not have any to begin with, but it does increase fuel usage percentage-wise for any division that already has it instead of decreasing it the way a regular logistics company would. Otherwise, compared to a logistics company, helicopter transports provide additional movement speed in most terrain types. Upgrading helicopter tranports also provides bigger supply usage reductions compared to upgrading logistics companies, though their percentage-wise increase to fuel usage remains. As their only downsides compared to logistics companies come from them increasing fuel usage instead of decreasing it, they are straight upgrades to regular logistics companies for divisions that would not otherwise use fuel, such as infantry or special forces divisions without any armored or motorized support companies.
Helicopters are able get a good vantage point of the battlefield regardless of the actual terrain, and thus make excellent forward scouts to provide accurate feedback to artillery barrages.

Helicopters equipped with transport pods or towing goods beneath them on a line can move supplies and equipment quickly and without regard for terrain. Getting stuck in the mud is a thing of the past!

Higher levels of infrastructure also allow supply from a hub to reach further, by reducing the drop-off in supply flow from the hub (to a maximum reduction in drop-off of 0.3 for level 5 infrastructure). Note that the level of infrastructure that matters is the level of infrastructure for state containing the province from which the supply is flowing. So, for example, if there are two states, a level five infrastructure state with a supply hub bordering a level one infrastructure state, the supply flowing from a province in the level five infrastructure state to a bordering province in the level one infrastructure state will flow as if it was level five infrastructure. However, supply flowing from a province in a level one infrastructure state to another bordering province in the same level one infrastructure state, will flow as if it was level one infrastructure.

Historically Costa Rica was one of the nations that made up the United States of Central America however following disputes with the central government would secede in 1838. In the following decades it would encourage German migration in order to create more plantations and boost its economy. In 1921 it would engage in a minor border conflict with ⟦0⟧ over the Coto region called the Coto War. Both Costa Rica and Panama struggled to acquire weaponry to equip their respective armed forces but still had their limited forces take up positions for a wider conflict. However it came quickly to an end when the ⟦1⟧ intervened with its navy and demanded both sides cease hostilities. The result in the end was that Costa Rica received the disputed region in the peace treaty that settled the border.

Historically Honduras was one of the stronger supporters for the reunification of the United States of Central America being an ally of ⟦0⟧ during that nations war to force Central America into reunification in 1885.

Historically Panama would gain independence from ⟦0⟧ in 1821 and at the same time entered into the confederation of Gran Colombia. Following the collapse of this confederation in 1831 it would remain a part of ⟦1⟧ though due to a chronic lack of investment in the region and cultural differences from the lack of any land based transport connections it would be a source of constant instability and revolts. This would culminate in 1903 when the ⟦2⟧ would intervene on the side of Panamanian separatists against the Columbian government during yet another revolt to recognize the independent nation of Panama in exchange for total control of the Panama Canal Zone under the Hay–Bunau-Varilla Treaty. In 1921 Panama would engage in a minor border conflict with ⟦3⟧ over their unclear borders at that time which would result in Panama ceding the Coto region to Costa Rica.

Historically speaking, ⟦0⟧ is the "legitimate founder" as after World War II with its homeland in ruins, its economy in shambles, its population depleted and its colonial empire breaking apart, France became desperate to avoid spiraling into a complete socio-economic meltdown and in 1956 the French government presented a proposal to form a Franco-British Union with the United Kingdom or simply joining the Commonwealth for aid. Both proposals fell through, and France instead turned to the defeated Axis Powers (Germany and Italy) of all nations and formed the European Coal and Steel Community alongside the Low countries to sustain itself, later reorganizing into the European Union.

Historically Venezuela was one of the nations that made up the confederation of Gran Colombia. However upset with increasing centralization of the government and lack of autonomy for the confederation member nations, Venezuela would secede in 1830.

Historically, ever since the power of the monarch had been curbed by the revision of the constitution in 1848, the Netherlands has been a democracy with a figurehead monarch. However, universal suffrage was not attained until 1917. The nation had long been practising a policy of neutrality, but with the upcoming German threat it has decided to re-militarize the nation, although far too late.

Historically, France elected to Form the Popular Front, the left-wing Democratic path. This puts Léon Blum in power and unlocks Reform the Labour Laws plus six more focuses that improve the economy and add free factories. Note that the Matignon Agreements can be repealed later for 50 PP but no other penalty. The right-wing Democratic path via Revive the National Bloc focuses on market reforms to fix the economy. Either way the priority is to get rid of your starting national spirits as soon as possible, especially Disjointed Government. Getting to Strengthen Government requires at least 350 days, or up to 490 via Revive the National Bloc and Confirm Eastern Commitments. A year after taking Strengthen Government, you can take Defensive Stratagems to finally remove Disjointed Government. This means France will be starved for political power until 1938.

Historically, it is a continuation of the many different polities that once existed in the area under the name of Livonia, tracing their lineage all the way back to the Livonian tribe of the Early Middle Ages before the area was Christianised. More specifically, the Kingdom of Livonia is most likely a restoration of either the Duchy of Livonia (which existed from 1561 to 1621) or the original Kingdom of Livonia (which existed from 1570 to 1578) or it could be interpreted as being connected to the long succession of Livonian governorates that existed from the 1620s to 1918 under Swedish, Polish and later Russian rule.

Historically, the Dutch nation attempted to stay Neutral in the upcoming conflict, but Germany had decided to invade the Netherlands on the 10th of May 1940, in order to bypass the French Maginot line. Like its neighbors, the Netherlands fell to the Germans and continued as a Government in Exile in London, while the queen and her family went to London. It engaged once more in the Asian theatre to fight off the invading Japanese from the Dutch East Indies, but failed and the Netherlands' biggest colony fell to the Japanese soon after its declaration of war against the Allies.

Historically, the Kingdom of Poland existed in various iterations from as early as 1025 AD until its demise in 1795. The kingdom was restored in a way as the semi-autonomous polity of Congress Poland, existing from 1815 to 1867, with an attempted real restoration during the November Uprisings of 1830-1831 and the January Uprising of 1864. After this, Poland's autonomy was severely curtailed and the Kingdom of Poland thereafter was mostly a formality, existing only on paper. After the collapse of the Russian Empire in 1917, the Kingdom of Poland was re-established by the German Empire and a Regency Council was inaugurated with the task of electing a king to the vacant throne. This ultimately never came to pass, as Germany was defeated by the Entente and signed an armistice on the 11th November 1918. The Regency Council of the newly formed Kingdom of Poland failed to crown a King before Marshal Józef Piłsudski declared the ⟦0⟧, which still exists in 1936.

Ideologically, the most optimal route would be to go Fascist or stay non aligned. If the player fights the Nationalists whilst the player are in the Axis, they have no faction to join, they get no aid (Volunteers/Lend-Lease), and the player can get German help. If the player fights the Republicans, they can potentially join the Comintern, dragging the player into a war with the Soviet Union. Assuming they have done "The Great Purge", Germany can defeat the Soviets, but the player has to manually Justify a War Goal on Poland so Germany has a land border with the Soviets. The war with the Soviets will be a long and costly slog that may last at least 3 years. Becoming Communist is an objectively bad idea. Firstly, later in the game, the player will end up at war with the Axis after Germany declares war on the Soviet Union. This will most likely lead to Germany seizing the entire Iberian Peninsula (Portugal and Spain), and its industry with it. Secondly, war with any other country will lead to an early World War between the Comintern and (For example) the Allies. This war would cripple the Soviet Union, and, without the Soviets, the entire Comintern will fall.

If all potential importers' trade influence with the exporter is identical, then they can will be able to access equal shares of the exporter's resources. However, if one country has far more trade influence with the exporter than others, it will be able to access a far greater share of the exporters. Similarly, if a country has far less trade influence with the exporter than others, its maximum potential share of the exporter's exported resources will be far lower. For example, if one country has 120 trade influence with an exporter and another has only 80, in a scenario where there is not enough resources to satisfy the trade desires of both countries, the first country gets priority access for up to 60% of the exporter's resources, potentially being able to muscle out the second country's trade down to 40% of the exporter's resources. If then a third country enters the picture with 200 trade influence, then they get priority access to up to 50% of the exporter's resources to match their share of the total amount of trade influence competing for a resource, dropping the priority access shares of the first and second countries to 30% and 20%, respectively.

If France is capitulated by a non-democratic Germany, and Germany is still at war with another major in the same faction as France, Germany can opt to set up an unofficial government in France - what government this is will depend on what ideology Germany is at the time. If Germany is Fascist, it will establish Vichy France. However, if Germany has restored the Kaiser, it will instead establish Bourbon France, although unlike what happens if France manually restores the monarchy, this Bourbon France will not have a king in charge (France will also become Bourbon France if it becomes a puppet of a non-aligned government). Alternatively, if France is Democratic and aligned with the UK (the UK can be any ideology), France can instead propose joining the two countries in the Franco-British Union - this decision will end the game for the French Player if the UK accepts, but in return, the British player will gain all existing French cores (this can include any gained through other methods), all French Units, Ships, Generals, Admirals, and equipment; while the Union can remain afterwards if the British player opts not to let France go independent when the Union is at peace, they will lose all French cores and generals/admirals if they choose to do so.

If Germany goes down its historic tree, France can opt to mobilize in response to the remilitarization of the Rhineland (taking this decision has a steep cost in political power and stability; note that France can only object if Germany completes the Remilitarize the Rhineland focus; if Germany remilitarizes the Rhineland by going to war, France cannot object). If the UK supports France, France (and any puppets France has at the time) will join the Allies, and if the Germans refuse to back down, when France goes to war, a civil war will break out. If the UK refuses to back up France, however, France can either opt to oppose Germany itself (which will also trigger a civil war) or it can back down. If Germany does back down in response to either instance, not only will the Rhineland remain demilitarized, but it will also give them a negative debuff that will lock off Anschluss for 1 year (additionally, when Germany does go to war, this will mean that the Rhineland will be unprotected by German troops for a while). Similarly, France can act differently in response to German demands for the Sudetenland than the UK; if the UK agrees to let Germany have the Sudetenland, France can either agree with the UK, which will also cancel its guarantee of Yugoslavia, or refuse to go along with the UK and form a faction with Czechoslovakia. However, if the UK refuses to let Germany have the Sudetenland, France can either opt to stay out of the conflict (which will cancel their guarantees of Czechoslovakia and Yugoslavia), or it can reaffirm its support (if the UK is not in a faction already but France is in one, the UK is added to France's faction and vice-versa; however, if both France and the UK are in separate factions, then France will guarantee Czechoslovakia). Similarly, if Germany overthrows Hitler and opts to restore the Kaiser, France can raise an objection to the Return of Kaiser Wilhelm II (the AI will usually limit its response based on how much tension Germany has generated); similar to the remilitarization of the Rhineland, the UK can opt to support or not support France, and Germany can either choose to continue ahead or compromise and instead install Wilhelm III as Kaiser. This will give them a similar debuff, but unlike the Rhineland Challenge Met debuff, none of Germany's focuses will be blocked.

If more than one country is fighting on the losing side of the war, the entire faction will surrender when the last ⟦0⟧ country in it surrenders (you can see which countries are considered majors on the world diplomacy screen). When this happens, the game will pause and a ⟦1⟧ will begin. The peace conference proceeds in stages based on the war effort expended by the victorious powers. So, for example, if the Allies defeat Germany and the ⟦2⟧ achieved the most in the war followed by the ⟦3⟧, the United States will have the first chance to make demands on the Germans, followed by the United Kingdom. Then, the next most significant victor(s) will make their demands.

If multiple contests erupt with the AI, it is worth sticking to demands for only one or two turns. This is because the player will start permanently losing some war score after the first turn of the contest and will incur opportunity costs on demanding other states. When there are multiple states contested, the AI will start forfeiting some of their demands at a rate of 1 or 2 per turn, but eventually the AI will stubbornly stick to a few demands and the player will face diminishing returns fighting for them.

If one is attempting to have the US become communist, the 13 states that broke away during the first civil war (Texas, Arkansas, Louisiana, Tennessee, Mississippi, Alabama, Georgia, Florida, South Carolina, North Carolina and Virginia) will break away; if one does not complete "Guarantee the American Dream" before hand, they will also lose the Midwest. As such, it is recommended that one beeline for said focus. Fortunately, you will not have your forces split when this war begins, so if you position your troops on the borders of the states that will break away, it will be very easy to move downwards and defeat them. Deploy some cavalry (5 divisions should be plenty) near Texas to secure the oil supplies - the capital can vary (sometimes it can be Richmond, VA; sometimes it can be Mobile, Alabama), but deploying 5 additional cavalry closest to where the capital is can help as well (if you train 2 sets of 5 divisions but don't deploy them, you should be fine). Use your navy to ensure naval superiority on the East Coast and stop naval invasions.

If one is in charge of a medium/large country (i.e., Germany, France): Get ahold of some army exp (through fighting in a war, exercising your troops, lend-lease, or sending an attache), and use that to design a template with a single artillery unit (anti-tank or anti-air will work just fine if you wish to use those instead). Train multiple copies of that unit, disband your entire army, and deploy the trained units at the start of the civil war. After your forces are split, change the divisions you kept to a different template. Because the AI will never change the template, this will make their army incredibly weak, and also give you a large number of units (which is helpful if you happen to have a civil war where, in addition to splitting the existing military, both sides will spawn new units).

If one is in charge of a small country (i.e., Greece, Bulgaria): train a single cavalry or motorized unit, and disband all other units. Deploy the unit and have it take all the victory points. While it is possible that the AI will train units by that point, it will not stop you from winning with this strategy as long as you keep on moving the cavalry/motorized unit.

If the United States progresses down the communist branch of its national focus tree and completes either the Full Desegregation or Union Representation Act national focuses, then an event titled "⟦0⟧" will trigger, serving as a warning that bad things are about to happen. This event is later followed by another one, titled "⟦1⟧", which is the gatekeeper event; when it triggers, it signals that the countdown to the civil war has begun. Over the course of the next 200 days, a series of random events will start triggering, causing Civilian and Military factories to be moved to the Confederacy's starting territory, generals to resign (removing generals), soldiers to desert (removing manpower), equipment to be stolen from the stockpile, and funds to be withheld from the government. Lastly, some states (that will revolt) will mobilize the National Guard, which will spawn divisions when the war breaks out.

If the United States progresses down the fascist branch of its national focus tree and completes either the ⟦0⟧ or ⟦1⟧ national focuses, then an event titled "⟦2⟧" will fire, eventually followed by another event titled "⟦3⟧". The latter event is the gatekeeper event, and once it fires, a 280-day countdown will start, culminating in the outbreak of civil war. If, however, both of the aforementioned focuses have been completed when the Ten-Million-March even fires, then the countdown is reduced to 180 days. Just as with the anti-communist version, a series of random events will trigger during the countdown, removing manpower, equipment, generals and moving factories. Additionally, sometimes worker strikes can occur, inflicting temporary penalties to industrial output and resources gain. Instead of mobilizing the National Guard, some states (that will revolt) will form citizen militias, which will then spawn divisions when the war breaks out.

If the US takes the focus "Unholy Alliance", and the Soviets accept them into the faction, the US is granted a decision that, when the USSR is at war, allows them to annex the USSR if the USSR ever gets a surrender threshold of 20% or lower as long as the US is in the Comintern (the US needs to be communist if it wishes to join the Comintern by clicking the "Join Faction" button, but it can take the focus even if it's democratic).

If trying to use a character that takes several bytes to write in the UTF-8 encoding, the game will only try to read the last byte of the character rather than the entirety of it. This may result in either of the previous errors, but it makes finding the cause much harder. For example, trying to use ⟦0⟧, where Ā has the code of U+0100, will result in the game throwing an error of ⟦1⟧, and trying to use ⟦2⟧, where ō has the code of U+014D, will result in the game throwing an error of ⟦3⟧ (as the character 'M' has the code of U+004D).

If you are going the naval route, build up Dockyards until you have a minimum of 40. You can get a little over 10 Dockyards for free via Focuses as well. Take advantage of the Convoys to Destroyers En Masse decision, which allows you to infinitely trade 40 Convoys for 10 Destroyers. You'll also need probably a minimum of ~20 Basic or Improved Light Cruisers filled out with Medium Battery and Secondary Turret modules (and Armor II) in addition to all the free destroyers you get (which are mainly there just to soak damage because they're awful). Your first engagement with the Royal Navy will probably be a wash - you'll lose a ton of the free destroyers and a small handful of Light Cruisers, while they will lose around 70-90% of their screens. That's fine. Go back and repair. In the next fight, you should basically wipe out the entire half of the Royal Navy that's assigned to defend the UK. This happens because without all those screens you destroyed in the first battle, their capital ships will be vulnerable to your crazy high Light Attack stats and they'll lose very badly.

The naval invasion will guarantee Yugoslavia will be at the peace conference. You will then go to war in the summer of 1941, and you should be able to get Leningrad, Karelia and Murmansk while the German Reich does most of the fighting.

If you go to war over Poland in mid-1939, the Axis can attack through three fronts: Alsace-Lorraine, Belgium after Germany conquers them, and Italy after they join Germany's faction. None of your other territory really matters, though you can place small forces to hold Corsica and Tunisia from the Italians. Alsace-Lorraine has level 10 forts so the Germans can't make any progress against two infantry divisions per tile. Belgium is dangerous because of the open terrain and the huge force that Germany will send this way. One option is to build forts to level 2 or 3 and then get Extend the Maginot Line to add 2 more forts to each tile. The Italian front has good defensive terrain and a weaker foe but supply is bad in Savoy, so two good choices are to build a supply hub close to the Italian border or to entrench a few tiles to the west, letting the Italians advance a little way into the unsupplied area.
