Incorrect path – This is commonly the cause if the game displays the filesize of the mod, but doesn't load it. The mod doesn't route to the file directly. This can sometimes be a cause of further subfoldering, such as if the mod is located in mod/my_mod/cool_mod, yet the user-specific .mod file contains path = "mod/my_mod". In this case, the files still exist and get loaded. However, the game, for example, expects focus trees in the /Hearts of Iron IV/common/national_focus/ folder. mod/my_mod/cool_mod/common/national_focus/ gets taken to be /Hearts of Iron IV/cool_mod/common/national_focus/ instead, as path = "mod/my_mod" doesn't knock off the /cool_mod/ folder. This is corrected simply by adjusting the path to be to the correct folder. Invalid path – The intended folder is correct, yet it's stated in a way that the game can't recognise. One of the ways of doing so is using backslashes for folder separations, such as path = "mod\my_mod". This is incorrect, as a single backlash gets taken to be an escape character instead. Using forward slashes as in path = "mod/my_mod" is correct. Another way of doing so is using special characters in the name, such as path = "C:/Users/Пример кириллицы/Documents/Paradox Interactive/Hearts of Iron IV/mod/my_mod". In this case, a special character is defined as one that takes more than 1 byte to write with UTF-8, not being present in ASCII's printable characters. This is commonly non-English language folder names, such as diacritics or non-Latin alphabets. In this case, it can be rerouted to a folder that does not contain special characters in the name, such as path = "D:/Hearts of Iron IV modding/my_mod". If the path to the user directory itself contains special characters, it's better to re-route the entire directory to another folder. To do so, edit the base game's /Hearts of Iron IV/launcher-settings.json file and change the folder specified under gameDataPath. After doing so, move the user directory's contents to that folder as to not lose save games and other information. The mod's path also needs to be adjusted properly. If the user directory has non-ASCII characters in the path to it, then all local mods stored there (as the default place to store them) will fail to be loaded and the in-game means will fail to open the error log, with a pop-up saying that the system cannot get access to the file. The default Steam installation folder has a path that will only have ASCII characters in it, making the Steam mods work as intended even if the user directory has non-ASCII characters in it.

Intel is particularly important in multiplayer, where otherwise somewhat predictable AI opponents are replaced with potentially very unpredictable human ones. Intel serves as one of the main ways with which to deal with that unpredictability, observing what other players are doing and anticipating what will be needed to fight them while it is early enough to make such decisions. Denying enemy intel has similarly elevated importance in multiplayer: while AI opponents cannot predict or anticipate a player's moves, human opponents can, so preventing them from seeing what you are doing until it is too late for them to prepare appropriate countermeasures can be crucial to long-term strategy.

Intuitively, the chance for the largest-valued focus to get picked consists of 2 mutually exclusive possibilities: the picked value between ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ is larger than ⟦2⟧ and the opposite: it is smaller. While it's theoretically possible that the same value will get picked for both, ⟦3⟧. The chance of the former is the first element of the sum: ⟦4⟧ . If that possibility is fulfilled, the element with the chance of ⟦5⟧ will get picked every time since other focuses can't get a higher value. If the latter possibility is met, which has the chance of ⟦6⟧ , each focus has an equal chance to be picked. Since there are ⟦7⟧ focuses in total, the chance gets divided by that number. That is the entire chance for the smaller-valued focuses, while it gets added to the larger-valued focus alongside the chance for the initial possibility.

This will position the focus relative to that focus, adding the ⟦2⟧ and ⟦3⟧ values to the other focus' position (after calculating that one's relative_position_id too). For example, if focus A has ⟦5⟧, focus B is positioned relative to focus A and has ⟦6⟧, then the focus B will be positioned, in total, 4 steps to the right and 6 steps down of the top-left corner. The game can behave unstably with an incorrect relative position ID. It is often useful to define related dummy tokenizable database entries, especially ideas, to represent arbitrary (possibly enumerable) custom datatypes. In most cases, ideas are preferable, however there can be uses for other token types, such as technologies if the code is to implement something that can't be done with a regular idea. The reason for idea preference is little to no downstream effects simply from existing, ease to define in bulk with minimal syntactic overhead, and ease to separate different custom datatypes by using custom idea categories and by placing the definitions for different custom datatypes in different files within ⟦0⟧. Decisions or technologies are common alternatives for custom datatypes with different usages, but generally datatypes other than these have too much downstream baggage (i.e. their very existence has consequences elsewhere, such as custom building types appearing automatically in certain UIs) to be worth using for dummy values.

Italian troops invaded Greece via Albania in October of 1940, but by November unexpectedly stiff resistance from the Greek Army turned the invasion into a humiliating disaster. In late November, the Greeks counterattacked, pushing the Italians back into Albania. Greek forces soon invaded Albania in December, but would later stop advancing and hold positions at key defending positions by January 1941 due to dangerously low supplies. The front would largely remain unchanged, save for another failed Italian offensive in March 1941. Greece would ultimately fall when Germany, fearful of substantial ⟦0⟧ intervention in the conflict, launched its own invasion from ⟦1⟧ on 6 April, 1941. German troops after three days of fight encountered fierce resistance and had little success breaching the undermanned Metaxas Line defending the Bulgarian border. Finally, German forces bypassed the Metaxas fortifications and crossed the Yugoslavian borders, overcame Yugoslav and Greek resistance and captured Thessaloniki on the 9th of April. The capture of Thessaloniki forced the defenders to surrender on the 10th of April and the Metaxas Line battle was over. Axis forces poured into the country. By 27 April, Athens had fallen, and by the end of the month the entire Greek mainland was captured. Crete fell a week later.

These factors make Italy a rewarding yet potentially overwhelming nation for inexperienced players.

Italy is an interesting country to play despite being the weakest of all starting Majors. It is unique in that it is the only nation that starts off at war with another nation in 1936, that being ⟦0⟧. Taking Ethiopia isn't a problem, but the war provides an easy early-game source of military experience for reformatting the Italian army divisions. Timing the end of the war is also important. End it too early and you likely will not be able to earn much experience for your generals and field marshals. End it too late and the war might just drain a large chunk of your manpower and/or equipment and the Spanish civil war might just start and end before you can finish the "⟦1⟧" national focus. While the Ethiopian war and Spanish civil war is ongoing, build up your military and industry, you will need them later. Some traits you may want to get with a small number of generals are Mountaineer, Desert Fox, Infantry Leader and Trickster, whilst getting them to level 6 if possible (and making them field marshals should you wish). With the pair of aforementioned terrain-based traits, you will be able to get the Adaptable trait, arguably one of the best that the game has to offer. Its 45% terrain penalty reduction makes attacking into finicky terrain that you'll inevitably have to fight through in a historical game much easier, and thus is very much advised to acquire whenever possible, not just when playing Italy.

Keep a close eye on logistics. You start with relatively few military factories compared to the size of your army. Shortages of Infantry Equipment and Support Equipment are common, tend to get worse during periods of heavy combat, and will degrade the effectiveness of your troops if left unchecked. It may be necessary to pause the fighting from time to time to cover the shortages. It helps somewhat to raise equipment reliability via Military Industrial Organization traits, and to add "Maintenance Company" battalions to division templates. If you are still having shortages after mid-1940, you can request lend-lease from ⟦0⟧, and the AI may offer you as much as 15k units of infantry equipment in a single shipment. Be warned that accepting a shipment of this size will tie up all your convoys for several months, during which time you will be unable to use them for either trade or supply (your armies in mainland China may suddenly find themselves out of supply and out of oil.)

Latvia achieved independence as a result of the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk, signed between Imperial Germany, Austria-Hungary and the Russian Provisional Government in March 1918. After the collapse of the Russian Provisional government and the rise of the Bolshevik communist regime, the Petrograd Soviet, seeking to prevent Baltic independence and spread the proletarian world revolution, invaded the Baltic region. Latvia joined forces with the rest of the Baltic States to defend its independence and was able to stop the Russian offensive. A peace treaty was signed in 1920 and Latvia's independence was recognized by the rest of the world after World War I. As part of the secret protocol of the Molotov-Ribbentrop pact, Eastern Europe was divided into spheres of interest by Germany and the ⟦0⟧. Latvia was in the Soviet zone and was occupied by the Soviet Union in 1940. This occupation was briefly interrupted in 1941 by Operation Barbarossa when Germany occupied the area, reorganizing the Baltic States into the "Reichskommisariat Ostland". The area was re-occupied by the Soviet Union in 1944-1945 and the Baltic States were annexed into the Soviet Union after the end of World War II and reorganized into the Estonian SSR, Latvian SSR and Lithuanian SSR. Latvia remained part of the Soviet Union until 1991 when it declared itself independent during the collapse of the Soviet Union.
Latvia has no alliances at the start of the game. However, they may join the Międzymorze if created by ⟦0⟧ or follow their own National Focus tree as of ⟦1⟧ to create or join the Baltic Union.

Like many other strategy games, holding shift ⟦0⟧ while right clicking sets a series of waypoints for selected units. They will choose the best path to get to each waypoint in succession. Like mentioned when discussing the focus tree, building a capable navy is essential for waring with your neighbors as to invade Central America or Hispaniola will require a fleet for naval invasions along with basic transport tech researched. Therefore, it may be a good idea to join a faction (like the Comintern when flipped communist) in order to access the "Technology Sharing" focus as well as completing the "Extra Research Slot" focus. Going after Venezuela may also be a good strategy as they have immense amounts of oil deposits scattered around the country.

Like naval units, air units operate over regions and are given specific missions relevant to the type of aircraft. Fighters can perform air superiority or interception missions, strategic bombers can target industry or infrastructure, tactical bombers can provide close support for land attacks, and so on. Lithuania broke free from the collapsing Russian Empire in 1918, along with the other Baltic States and found itself quickly in conflict to defend its newly gained independence. Lithuania fought against the Russian SSR (precursor to the ⟦0⟧) alongside Poland and the other Baltic States and was able to stop the Russian grand offensive of 1918-1919. After beating back the Bolsheviks, Lithuania, along with the other Baltic States, fought an internal war against the West Russian Volunteer Army (essentially a leftover of the Imperial Russian Army) which had officially joined arms with Alexander Kolchak's White Russia in the Russian Civil War (Which opposed Baltic Independence). After exterminating any remaining Russian military units on its territory, Lithuania found itself at war with newly-independent Poland. The reason for the war was a territorial dispute, the Vilnius region had been assigned to Lithuania by the Russians in the peace treaty they have signed after the Baltic Wars of Independence, but later it was occupied by Poland. In 1926, Antanas Smetona took authoritarian power during coup d'etat.
Lithuania can no longer get Poland into a Personal Union without Lithuania being fully independent.

Lithuania is one of the most difficult minor nations to play, as it is a target of both the German Reich (who claims Memel) and the Soviet Union (who claims everything else). This makes Lithuania's position very precarious, as it cannot fight either power on its own. Since the USSR is by far the greatest threat to its survival, Lithuania must seek to ally itself with either the Axis or the Allies until it can stand on its own two feet.

Lithuania is situated within the Baltics, a region that is geographically located in Northern Europe. The country has land borders with ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧, and Germany. Additionally, Lithuania possesses a modest coastline along the Baltic Sea.

Located to Japan's Southwest, ⟦0⟧ presents a relatively early conquest goal for Japan. The Japanese national focus tree contains the necessary focuses to grant a war goal against China very early on in the game and this makes China a perfectly logical conquest option in the early game. When taking on China, the Japanese player must be aware of two crucial facts: first, China has the second highest (highest after unification) starting core population in the game and this grants it a near-bottomless manpower supply. As such, a war of attrition is not an option for Japan as Japan will run out of manpower long before China. Instead, the recommended path is for Japan to strike fast and strike hard, using equipment such as artillery and either heavy fighters or tanks to deal maximum damage to the Chinese forces. Second, it is recommended that the player strike China from multiple directions by opening new fronts through naval invasions. Once the war starts, two possible option for additional strikes would be a naval invasion of the Shandong peninsula through Qingdao, followed by a rush inland to cut off supply line to Beijing or an invasion of Southern China to capture a large portion of China's resources.

Logical focuses for war are your weak southern neighbors; especially one mainland state Ecuador(South Colombia) and Peru. Venezuela is the next target later on, as they are simply East Colombia and must be reincorporated. Another set of possible targets that have little unlocked slots but major aluminum resources are the Guyanas, from west to east colonies of ⟦0⟧ (British Guyana), ⟦1⟧ (Suriname) and ⟦2⟧ (French Guiana). While they are fighting with the Axis in Europe and Africa, their colonies are sparsely occupied by minor troops and can be easily taken with Naval Invasions, just as Jamaica, Trinidad and Belize (British Mexico). Your northwestern neighbor Panama is split into two parts with the US occupied but very important Panama Canal in between, a good strategy for the longer term. Because of this barrier, you need Naval Invasions for the northern part of Panama. There are only three US divisions stationed at the crucial Panama Canal, but they are extremely strong in Attack (⟦3⟧ and ⟦4⟧) and Defense and trying to conquer the Canal brings you into war with the far superior United States. To get to conquer the Panama Canal you also need a lot of naval and air superiority.

Maintenance companies are your best friend. They should be the very first thing your research, and producing enough support equipment is the most important thing after infantry equipment, even more important than artillery - because they allow you to steal Japans artillery... and pretty much everything else. This will prove to be of immense value, as your own war industry is seriously lacking and won't see too much improvement for a while. Therefore being able to re-use dropped japanese equipment is a godsend. Research the level 2 update once it becomes available to increase your capture ratio to a whopping 10%. Same thing theoretically goes for level 3 of that technology in 1942, though chances are you won't have to. By that point Japan will likely have run out of steam and also be fighting on mutiple fronts, completely losing the war of attrition.

The reliability bonus is shown as a "Reliability Bonus" in the division view, rather than being calculated for each division and then recalculated; as a result, all calculations for this company must be done outside the game.

Maqsud Shah (known to the Chinese as the Hami Wang, to his subjects as Khan Maqsud or Sultan Maqsud and to the Europeans as the King of the Gobi), was a devout muslim ruling over a petty oasis kingdom from an ancient and ramshackle palace in Hami, one of three towns making up the capital of Kumul proper, known to the Chinese as Huicheng. He had a bodyguard consisting of 40 Chinese soldiers armed with Type 88 and Type 24 Mauser rifles and had a Chinese garrisson billeted in the fortified town as well as a Uyghur militia throughout the countryside. The third town in his domain was the New City or Xincheng. By 1928, it was estimated that Maqsud Shah ruled over some 25.000-30.000 Kumuliks, a far cry from the tens of millions once ruled over by his Mongol ancestors. He was responsible for levying taxes, dispensing justice and so forth, through an administration consisting of 21 Begs or local governors.

Mechanical change: This changes how some mechanic works by continuously checking for the game rule being set in-game. For example, the game rule to hide obsolete ⟦0⟧ branches does so by including a check for the game rule being set in the ⟦1⟧. These two subsets are particularly notable:
mechanized equipment can now be upgraded in four different areas: Armor, Engine, Reliability, Cost
Mechanized forces backed up by fast light tanks and armored cars can probe for weak spots and hit the enemy where they are most vulnerable.

Mechanized infantry is infantry equipped with armored personnel carriers (APCs) or infantry fighting vehicles (IFVs) for transport and combat. Mechanized infantry is distinguished from motorized infantry in that its vehicles provide a degree of protection from hostile fire, as opposed to soft-skinned wheeled vehicles (trucks or jeeps) for motorized infantry.

Mechanized technologies focus on improving ⟦0⟧ units and can benefit from motorized technology bonuses. Compared to ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧ are slower, more expensive, and more fuel-intensive (though they are still much faster than ordinary ⟦3⟧), but they have far greater hardness and provide a lot more defense and HP. Their production costs can also be potentially through designing a variant using ⟦4⟧, which, when coupled with how few equipment losses they suffer thanks to their high HP, can actually make them more affordable in practice than ⟦5⟧ once the combat casualties start rolling in. Although their offensive stats lack compared to tanks', with enough upgrades, ⟦6⟧ can also be surprisingly capable on the offense and can even go toe-to-toe with enemy tanks when used alongside ⟦7⟧ units.

Mechanized warfare is a form of combat that requires fast decision making and fast movement of troops and supplies. If our tanks are to carry modern weapons and enough armor to survive on the battlefield, they require powerful engines to keep up with the motorized infantry.

MEFO Bills system provides drastically different mechanics based on the path you choose that'll suit players with different playstyle. From a more relaxed, late-game booming strategy that allows you to slowly build up, to a more aggressive, early rushing strategy with the aim of crushing the opponents before they have time to grow.

MEFO bills were promissory notes created by Hjalmar Schacht in 1934 to enable the government to fund rearmament, acting through the balance sheet entity ⟦0⟧tallurgische ⟦1⟧rschungsgesellschaft to hide this rearmament from French and British eyes. It also allowed the government to run a great deficit and procure billions of Reichsmarks worth of funds without devaluing the currency. These bills were supposed to mature in six months, after which their recipients would have to be paid and would cause mass inflation, but historically the German government delayed the problem by extending the bills indefinitely. This contributed to part of the reason Germany initiated the war as soon as they did with the ultimate goal of obtaining enough resources for economic self-sufficiency.

There ⟦0⟧ effects that trigger a government in exile, but using them when a country is completely annexed makes the player automatically lose the game. In this way, using the command tag = <country tag> on the debug mode will not cause the player to change to the exiled government: it would trigger a message error ⟦1⟧ . Modifiers are factors multiplied against the state value to either increase or decrease the total cost. Factors less than 1.0 will decrease the cost, while factors greater than 1.0 will increase the cost. Thus, a modifier of 1.2 represents a 20% increase while a modifier of 0.8 represents a 20% decrease. The ⟦0⟧ displayed in the demand tooltip (i.e., the 'Multiplied by' value) is computed by multiplying all active modifiers by each other. This product is then multiplied by the ⟦1⟧ to arrive at the war score cost for the state. The breakdown of constituent cost modifiers is displayed in the demand tooltip when hovering over a demand in the peace conference by holding the ⟦2⟧ key.

Most missions are conditional, in that planes will only fly if there is a known target at the time a wing mission is being chosen. Some missions will always fly. Targets are checked in each of the air zones assigned to the air wing, checking provinces within range of the air wing. If there are no appropriate targets for a mission type, the mission selection process will continue to the next lower priority mission. The first mission with a valid condition is the only mission flown by that air wing during that mission opportunity. Since many of the conditions during play are dynamic, wings may fly different missions at different types, producing multiple types of results. If one of the assigned missions has a condition that's "Always executes", no later mission in the list will ever be executed by that wing.

Nationalist campaigns into communist territory in southern China were interrupted from 1929 through 1931, when Japanese expansion into Manchuria (the Mukden Incident and subsequent territorial concessions) and Northern China halted nationalist offenses for a time. Mao's forces declared independence as an otherwise unrecognized ⟦0⟧ existing in various pockets throughout China. 1932 to 1933 saw limited success for the KMT, though new failure to halt ⟦1⟧ forced demilitarization of the area around Beijing. But in 1934, careful encircling maneuvers crushed communist pockets, leading Mao's forces to exile on the Long March, nearly obliterating the communists in the process. However, the surviving communists reorganized in Yan'an in far northern China during 1935-1936. There, Mao's conviction in communism's inevitability strengthened. The civil war was temporarily halted in 1937 when ⟦2⟧ invaded ⟦3⟧ and the CPC and KMT formed the Second United Front to battle the Japanese, but almost immediately resumed after the latter's surrender, ending with the Republic of China's retreat to Taiwan and the establishment of the People's Republic of China under Mao on the mainland.

Neither route is "better", there's trade-offs to both. Naval will take you longer because realistically you probably won't be able to take the Royal Navy in a fight before 1943 safely (depends slightly on how many Dockyards you build), but you can paradrop as early as mid-1941 if you're doing it right. The advantage of the naval route is that you can stop all of the convoy raiding and actually trade with other countries and consistently supply your troops. Having a strong airforce will make pushing through the USA much easier after adding in some CAS, but getting a landing point in the Americas can be hard. Sometimes, ⟦0⟧ will still be alive and will have joined the ⟦1⟧ (they join in 1941 or 1942 and often hold out well against naval invasions because of the terrain). You can use them to paradrop into ⟦2⟧ and start your invasion of North America.

Nepal starts in a difficult position surrounded by giants such as China and British Raj, Therefore there is limited expansion opportunity. They have very weak industrial base, so rushing industrial focus is recommended. The goal is to join the Comintern and flip to fascist(to get better puppets). After taking Tibet and Bhutan, justify on Xibei San Ma. Calling the USSR prevents Sinkiang and Communist China from joining the war, or at the very least makes them join later (this will ensure they do not take your warscore, which would lower the amount of states you can take in the peace conference). Meanwhile, other Chinese overlords will most likely join the war. After they capitulate, puppet Communist China and give them the states. Since the puppet will have cheaper war score, and Japan has yet to puppet China, they will take less lands. Now you have a big puppet with lots of manpower. Declare war on China and finish the war. when the war is won, give your Chinese puppet the land in china. Now go on conquering Afghanistan and Iraq. Germany will declare on the USSR (with historical AI on historical AI) so decide which side to join. Sometimes the UK will invite you to the Allies if you are in the same war. How much you can do now will depend on your skill.

Nesting a boundable variable. Introduced in patch 1.15, boundable variables allow modders to define custom variables for use in localisation keys, functioning similarly to internal variables. These can be assigned within any effect, trigger block, or on a scripted GUI. For example, by using a loacalisation key like: ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧ in this case would be a custom boundable variable that can be defined elsewhere by the modder. This provides significant flexibility for dynamic localisation that adapts to gameplay conditions. For further details on defining and binding these variables, refer to the ⟦2⟧ section.

Nesting a strictly internal variable. This is particularly common within base game's localisation that corresponds to game mechanics rather than database entries, such as ⟦0⟧. In these cases, the specified internal variable only exists within the scope of that localisation key and cannot be used anywhere else.
Nesting other localisation keys. For example, ⟦0⟧ will show up in-game as ⟦1⟧, assuming that ⟦2⟧'s definition is unchanged from the base game.

Italy and Germany will certainly come in aid, but unlike in their case, the required lands must go into Croatian hands, including Vojvodina. Thus, Yugoslavia will grind their troops mainly with Croatia and time to time try to outmaneuver them directly from the Slovene and Croatian soil, prior entering to Vojvodina. Italy will flank them from the left, thus making it easier to encircle them if the Croatian troops are faster. Push from Bosnia and spearhead into Moravia and Montenegro. The Axis will try to attack Belgrade, so it is better to pin down some troops before they reinforce the defense. With Moravia and Serbia onto the Axis hands, be sure to clean every enemy troop that is inside Yugoslavia and that their lands pass onto Croatia.

Next up will be Chile. Be warned though no matter which other neighbor you attack next, it will be more difficult. Chile has among the strongest infantry division templates in South America at the very start of the game, and being only a few tiles wide you may have to deal a long war as you take the country one tile at a time as you make your down to the capital. In essence Chile will do the same thing to you as what you want to do with the Peruvians. Alternatively you could try to attack Argentina however it has larger armies and more manpower meaning in order to win you need finish the war as quickly as possible before it can produce more divisions. It is probably worth producing paratroopers for these options as you can land forces behind their lines to either pull forces off their front or conversely to pin down forces so they can't reinforce divisions your frontline army can defeat. It is strongly advisable to not attempt to attack Brazil unless you have conquered at least two other neighboring nations to gain more manpower and factories. Brazil at some point, will certainly attack you, by focus related events, and you have to make sure you are not in a war with any other nation, or if you have dealt with Chile and Paraguay respectively, you will have the chance to occupy Acre, albeit ending your National Regression de-buff.

Next, go down the Little Entente sub-branch towards Neutralize Hungarian Threat. When you start that focus, there is a 50% chance that Germany will guarantee ⟦0⟧. If this happens, you will need to either restart the entire run, or save scum to a save file taken before you started the focus. If save scumming, recruit a new army officer right after starting the focus to reset your RNG roll. Assuming Germany did not guarantee them, declare war on ⟦1⟧ and use your air force and divisions to encircle all Hungarian divisions to maximize your XP gains. In the peace deal, puppet ⟦2⟧, take all their ⟦3⟧ as war reparations, and take all their resource rights. With the air XP gained from this war, you can now design a decent fighter plane. With your ⟦4⟧, continue to do the “A Divided Nation” decisions, and also buy Partial Mobilization, Army Defense Expert, Ground Support Expert, attaché to ⟦5⟧. You can do more of your political tree, but make sure to do Ally Austria by the end of 1937 to prevent ⟦6⟧ from getting annexed by Germany with their Anschluss focus. In 1938, continue with political and industrial focuses, as well as focuses that give you manpower. National Defense Act is a good one to prioritize as it reduces the cost for conscription laws and boost military factory construction speed. After doing some of those manpower focuses, you should have enough available manpower to fulfil the 425.00k men in the field in order to complete the “Ready for Anything” decision in the Balance of Power. Improve relations with ⟦7⟧ and ⟦8⟧ and do the focuses to ally them before the end of the year, which is when the Munich Conference event usually starts. It is important to note that you must complete the focuses Truth Prevails and Forming a Federation before the Munich Conference, as you will be locked out of them once your cosmetic tag switches.

Norway attempted to stay neutral in World War II (like all other Nordic Countries) and remained so until the 9th of April 1940, when Germany invaded both ⟦0⟧ and Norway as part of Operation Weserübung. Operation Weserübung was intended to secure access to Norway's coastline and ports for the Kriegsmarine to use as well as ensuring the safe transportation of Swedish iron ore to Germany. In 1942, Germany established a puppet regime in Norway, known as the ⟦1⟧ or ⟦2⟧, headed by Vidkun Quisling, party chairman of the ⟦3⟧ political party, Norway's fascist party. After the death of Adolf Hitler, the Flensburg Government (successor state to Nazi Germany) drew up plans to withdraw the remnants of the Wehrmacht into Norway and Denmark, establishing those countries as a national redoubt and last holdout against the Allies. Norway remained under German occupation until May 8, 1945.

Norway is a minor nation to play, as it is a target of the Third Reich that will eventually annex or puppet them during Operation Weserübung. Despite the naval distance, between these two nations, a scripted civil war that will soon or later will be reinforced, and Norway's obsolete forces debuff makes Norway's position very precarious, as it cannot fight either power on its own. Since the Third Reich is by far the greatest threat to its survival, Norway must seek to ally itself with either the Allies or a domestic faction with Sweden until it can stand on its own two feet.

Norway is located in northern Europe on the Scandinavian peninsula. It is dominated by the Scandinavian mountains, which separates Norway from its neighboring country ⟦0⟧. Norway does have plains and forested areas, mostly to the southeast and the northernmost part.

Detailed information for subsequent generations will be found in ⟦0⟧ and for a comparison of equipment of equivalent generation: ⟦1⟧. Generally non-combat statistics are defined per battalion. But combat statistics are a function of equipment and thus not static. Additionally, battalions add modifiers to its equipment. For example, a Marine combat battalion adds +30% Breakthrough to its infantry equipment while an artillery support company has a -40% Soft Attack, -40% Hard Attack, -40% Defence, and -40% Breakthrough to its artillery equipment. If a battalion uses multiple types of equipment, the stats are a sum of all the equipment used. For example, Mechanized battalions use both Weapon and Mechanized equipment (with a 10% bonus to Weapon Soft Attack and 500% bonus to Weapon Hard Attack). Support Equipment adds nothing to combat stats.

If you want to stall a little longer, you can take Uruguay, Venezuela (This may drag you into WWII, so I would skip them until after). After that, if Germany's still going strong, join the Axis and unite South and Central America. Now for the army, start training the cheapest infantry (consisting of 3 infantry) divisions in batches of 3. Convert all your infantry brigades to this template. Later convert 6 of them to the marine template.

Now for the counterattack. You should have a ton of army XP by now, so invest in creating a division template with line and support artillery (which you need to research); a standard 7/2 template does the job. Gradually convert your weaker divisions into these offensive divisions, and make sure you have enough manpower either by upping your conscription law or by going down the Nationalism branch in your focus tree. Superior Firepower should be your doctrine here, since Italy has more manpower than you and your only advantage relies on breaking their front before they can reinforce it. Once you could mass around 7-8 divisions with artillery, and have sufficient manpower and equipment, you can strike them - usually by early to mid 1938 you have enough equipment for an offensive.

Now for the final part, make sure you have enough divisions to hold the Axis for around a week. Without massive losses to the ⟦0⟧, the German army will be quite big. Build forts if you think your line is too weak to hold. Finally, since you asked and got military access to both Germany and ⟦1⟧ during your war with the ⟦2⟧, you can simply walk some divisions into ⟦3⟧ and have them sit in one of the required states. They will need to be able to hold for about a week, so make sure you send enough divisions and also put a few on a port for safekeeping.

Now is a good time prepare any additional cheese you might want to use to make the civil war easier (e.g. deleting your starting army, creating a template containing one line anti-air battalion, putting as many as possible into training and then adding another anti-air battalion to the template to ensure that your opponent in the civil can't deploy any divisions by binding all of their manpower).

Now is a good time to take the focus Infiltration. Once you think the war is nearly won, with a few medium sized ⟦0⟧ patches, pause, delete a unit and take an infiltration decision. This will take 60 days. Remove the ⟦1⟧ patches during that time. As you do that, get divisions ready for the war with ⟦2⟧. When ⟦3⟧ white-peaces the Japanese, if done correctly, You will take Manchuria and Mengkukuo. Place divisions there. After the 60 days take the infiltration decision that gets you to war with China. It will take another 60 days. When you are at war with ⟦4⟧, push quickly until their divisions are met then stall a bit while pushing not as quickly. This is also a good time to take ⟦5⟧, ⟦6⟧, and ⟦7⟧ as they will join the Chinese United Front because they are non-aligned. ⟦8⟧, ⟦9⟧ and the rest of the middle east is good too if desired. However, ⟦10⟧ may be difficult because of the thin mountain border. Justify on 2 of them at a time. Be aware that they might join the Allies instead. When desired, capitulate and annex all of ⟦11⟧.

Now it is time to take the Triumph in Africa focus, once it completes go to the Balance of Power and take all the decisions which push the power to the left (red). Keep going down the focus and complete Convene the Grand Council. This allows you to hire the advisor which increase non-aligned popularity. Follow up with Depose Mussolini focus. You can detour and get your 5th research slot as well as The New Emperor of Ethiopia and Topple Amhara Rulers focuses if you wish. Before you take the Monarchia d'Italia focus, there are a couple of things you want. Take Ministero della Cultura Popolare and Believe, Obey, Fight focus just after it since you cannot take these focuses if you are no longer ⟦0⟧, you may also want to complete the Security Militias branch next as it unlocks a support company and some other bonuses which you will keep later on but since this increases ⟦1⟧ popularity, you might as well do these just before turning ⟦2⟧. Also you want to take the Foreign Affairs branch until you reach Albanian Occupation to get ⟦3⟧. One final wrinkle to be aware of is that Monarchia d'Italia switches your ideology and that automatically cuts the hard-earned compliance in all your non-core territories, including Ethiopia, in half (but you get 10% back as a hidden focus reward), and it removes the "Vittorio Emanuele III, Emperor of Ethiopia" national idea, which substantially reduces compliance growth rate. Take Monarchia d'Italia when you are done. Hire the advisor which increase political power gain if you wish.

Now the Allies leader control has been taken by USA. And obviously the next war wont be with the French Opposition in Africa or Middle East, but rather going for the Americas. Certainly Greenland is in Allied possession, and to provide a proper naval invading base, it is best that Greenland is taken first. Same tactic established, naval supremacy first, and a couple of troops landing on Greenlandic soil. After that the next is Newfoundland. The land itself isnt connected by land and it cant be reinforced by Canadian or American troops. Which is another safe landing with a little resistance, if there is any, to ensure a proper and easier naval invasion on the North American soil. Next stop is to land on Halifax, there is a guaranteed resistance, but less defended than the US coasts, and in a good reason to take the Halifax strip first. Canadas capitulation comes as a second priority, maintain a border with them and pour the rest of the troops south to reach in a surprise attack on the US soil. Take the entirety of New England, rush to Washington DC and proceed to take the entirety of your troops and your fight to the West Coast until US capitulates. Once it is done, Canada will be less of a problem, therefore try to occupy them next before they liberate the US. With the Peace Conference next, take and annex back lands that were lost to Free France, and annex Canada and USA back together.
Now the army theater groups will show the reinforcement priority.

Now the challenge is to capitulate Germany without depleting your army too drastically before the summer of 1940, which is when the Soviet Union is going to declare on Latvia and/or Lithuania and you'll have to fight the Soviets. By then you should have all your forces already at the eastern border (with one army guarding the Baltic coast against naval invasions.)

Now the control of the French lands has been taken by Free France. And obviously the next war wont be in Africa or Middle East, but rather chasing the Axis back to their capital. Certainly, Germany has the largest chunk of stolen French land. To provide a proper liberation, it is best that Germany is taken out of commission. Go for the Lowlands; liberating Belgium, Luxembourg and the Netherlands. Avoid going for the river protected cores, as they are costly to take in terms of manpower. Once it is done, pin, rush and outmaneuver the German units, encircling them in the process until reaching Berlin. Next stop is to bring the fight to Italy. Cut through the Franco-Italian border south of Switzerland while also pushing south through Germany. If you have troops in French Algeria and/or you took Libya, naval invade from across the Mediterranean. Parts of the Balkans will resist you, but they are less defended. Keep in mind that Hungary is in the faction too, and their capitulation comes as a second priority. Do not go for the Balkans yet, solely take the entirety of North Italy, rush to Rome while your Mediterranean troops push north from Naples to Rome. While the fight is occurring, Hungary will be less of a problem due to split attention with the Soviets. Try to assist the Allies next before they liberate the Balkans. With the Peace Conference next, reclaim land that was lost to Vichy France and Italy, and take extras if needed.

Now you can reform the Kalmar Union. Wait until WW2 (get a Non-aggression pact with the Axis) and justify on France. When Germany declares war on the Benelux (the Netherlands should have been annexed so you don't have to worry about Germany coming for you here), you can simply blast through Belgium and into France. You might need to join the Axis to have proper supply. Naval invade the United Kingdom and bag them up in London and take the rest of the isle. If possible, launch a naval invasion into the Isle of Man so you can reform the North Sea Empire right before the Peace Deal to take the English lands for a very cheap price. In the peace deal, focus on Canada (to attack USA), Guyanas (for Aluminium), Metropolitan France and Corsica and all of the British cores (for industry), Malaysia and Ceylon (for rubber and resources and to deny Germany of them), and whatever else you can get. You should be able to get them.

Now you have enough manpower and factories to build a powerful enough army to defeat the Axis. Depending on your skill level it might be smart to first secure your southern flank by conquering/puppeting ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ (and if you aren't in a hurry ⟦2⟧ as well). Your best chance to attack the Axis successfully is when they are busy in the ⟦3⟧. However, do remember that since the Allies are gone this Axis is more powerful.

Now you have Ryti in charge. Ban ⟦0⟧ immediately. Complete the Political Unity focus and then assign the ⟦1⟧. He gives you +200 Weekly Manpower (well over a 100% raw increase). His ⟦2⟧ support buff is completely countered by our ban, which allows us to "safely" have him as an advisor anyway. Grab all the focuses now in the political side of the tree that give buffs to Public Trust (except Collaboration with the Left) and take the Entice the Masses decision as soon as you can. This decision will come back in a year and taking it a second time usually pushes you into the highest level of Public Trust, which gives a recruitable population bonus and the OP National Spirit ⟦3⟧. Use your last open advisor slot to grab the ⟦4⟧, as his industry buffs are incredible. You can replace the ⟦5⟧ now and fill out the rest of the Military High Command with your personal picks.

Now you just sit and wait. (You can even do the focus for the Continuation War and you'll be invited to come along when the German Reich attacks the ⟦0⟧ in 1941. It's risky - you ⟦1⟧ lose some states this way - but it's more fun than sitting and waiting until 1944.)

Now, arrange your Mexican invasion army and your Central American divisions along the border with ⟦0⟧. As Colombia has a pretty weak army, this shouldn't be too hard. Quickly invade them and rush their capital with your divisions. While you invade Colombia, be sure to begin justifications on ⟦1⟧. Don't justify on ⟦2⟧ or ⟦3⟧ as they could join the Axis, and don't justify on ⟦4⟧ as they could join the Comintern. After Colombia falls, invade Ecuador and capitulate them. Now pause your expansion here for the moment and return to focusing internally.

Now, if you decide to wait, then your focus should be building up an elite army made up of small, quick, and flexible special forces units- marines, or mountaineers work well. NVIDIA's Texture Tools Exporter for Photoshop Open the heightmap and change the image mode to RGB, save a copy menu -> select the NVIDIA exporter's DDS format. In Image Type, select "Normal Map : Tangent Space". In "Height Source", select either "Max RGB" or "Average RGB" and in "Height Generation", check "Wrap" and "Invert Y". The "Filter Type" can be changed at will, look at the preview to see the results. "Scale" is the most important factor that will change the general look of the map, as this controls the intensity of the Normal Map. The larger the Scale, the "bumpier" the map becomes. At lower levels, this makes the generated map empty. Set "Alpha Field" to "Unchanged" and check "Normalize". Then open the saved DDS file and export to the BMP format.

On 1 April 1941, Rashid Ali al-Gaylani and members of the Golden Square staged a coup d'état and overthrew the government of 'Abd al-Ilah. During the subsequent Anglo-Iraqi War, the United Kingdom invaded Iraq for fear that the Rashid Ali government might cut oil supplies to Western nations because of his links to the Axis powers. The war started on the 2nd of May, and the British, defeated the forces of Al-Gaylani, forcing an armistice on the 31st of May.

On 1 September 1939, German troops invaded ⟦0⟧, precipitating war with the Allies. On 2 September, the Emergency Powers Act 1939 was introduced to grant government control of the economy and other sweeping powers.

On 1 September 1939, the day of the German invasion of the Free City of Danzig, Forster signed a law declaring the Free City to be incorporated into Germany. On the same day, Hitler signed a law declaring the law signed by Forster to be German law and the Free City of Danzig was officially incorporated into Germany.
On 2 November 1938 the First Vienna Award separated territories from Czechoslovakia, including southern Carpathian Rus', that were mostly Hungarian-populated and returned them to Hungary.

On 24 April 1916, the “Easter Rising” armed rebellion sought an independent Irish Republic. It had little public support at the time, but Britain's heavy-handed and indiscriminate response to it shifted Irish opinion, beginning a cycle of escalating “physical-force republicanism” and UK reprisals against combatants and civilians alike. This fueled the political rise of the republican Sinn Féin party and its military wing the Irish Republican Army.

On 30 October 1918, following the collapse of the Ottoman Empire, Imam Yahya Muhammad of the al-Qasimi dynasty declared northern Yemen an independent sovereign state. In 1926, Yahya proclaimed the Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen, becoming both a temporal king as well as a (Zaydi) spiritual leader, and won international recognition for his new state, such as with the Kingdom of Italy, entering into the Italo-Yemeni Treaty in 1926, and with Soviet Union, entering into the Soviet-Yemeni Treaty in 1928. In 1934 ⟦0⟧ would declare war on Yemen over disputed territories that Yemen occupied in the Northeast. While Yemeni soldiers would prevent the Saudi Arabian army from overrunning the kingdom, the better British equipped Saudi Arabian army would successfully occupy the disputed territories which Saudi Arabia would receive in the Peace Treaty of Taif thus ending the war.

On 31 December 1943, the Danish–Icelandic Act of Union expired after 25 years. Beginning on 20 May 1944, Icelanders voted in a four-day plebiscite on whether to terminate the personal union with Denmark, abolish the monarchy, and establish a republic. The vote was 97% to end the union, and 95% in favour of the new republican constitution. Iceland formally became a republic on 17 June 1944, with Sveinn Björnsson as its first president.

On August 6, 1945, the ⟦0⟧ dropped a nuclear bomb on Hiroshima, flattening the center of the city. Late in the evening of August 8, according to the Yalta agreements, the ⟦1⟧ declared war on Japan, and shortly after midnight on August 9, attacked Manchukuo and Mengjiang. Only hours later, the Americans dropped a second nuclear bomb on Nagasaki, destroying a small portion of it. The total shock of these events forced Emperor Hirohito to intervene and compel the big six to agree on the terms of ending the war, taken by the Allies in the Potsdam Conference. After several days of backroom negotiations and failed attempts to destroy the stockpiles of biological and chemical weapons of Unit 731 in Manchuria, which were captured by Soviet paratroopers, and the collapse of the Kwantung Army, in August 15, Hirohito addressed the nation by radio and announced the surrender of Japan. The signing ceremony of the Act of Capitulation took place on September 2 aboard the United States Navy battleship USS Missouri (BB-63).

On historical, Finland deploys their general Aksel Airo in mid '37. From here, you just have to keep him encircled & make sure the HQ doesn't kill itself before ~1938 - at around this time, Finland should promote Airo despite being encircled, and then you can capture him. On September 1, 1920, Greater Lebanon, or Grand Liban, was officially established under ⟦0⟧ control as a League of Nations Mandate, following the terms outlined in the proposed Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon. Greater Lebanon united the regions of Mount Lebanon, North Lebanon, South Lebanon, and the Bekaa, with Beirut as its designated capital. These specified boundaries later evolved into the present-day configuration of Lebanon. This arrangement was later ratified in July 1922. The Lebanese Republic was officially proclaimed on September 1, 1926, with the adoption of a constitution inspired by the ⟦1⟧ constitution on May 23 of the same year. While a Lebanese government was established, the country continued to be under ⟦2⟧ control.

On September 18, 1931, the Kwantung Army of ⟦0⟧ staged a false flag operation as a pretext to invade northeastern China in what became known as the Mukden Incident, leading to the swift occupation of northeastern China and the subsequent creation of the puppet state of ⟦1⟧ in 1932. A period of relative peace ensued for the next few years, until it was broken by ⟦2⟧ with a full-scale invasion in 1937 after the Marco Polo Bridge Incident. The Nationalists and Communists set aside hostilities and formed the Second United Front against Japan. ⟦3⟧ lasted until 1945 with the unconditional surrender of ⟦4⟧, following the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, and the Soviet invasion of ⟦5⟧. The Chinese Civil War, however, would reignite almost immediately thereafter, with major hostilities lasting from 1946 until 1950, after Communist forces had taken control of mainland China and the Republic of China had retreated to Taiwan. To this day, although combat has ceased, a peace treaty has never been signed, and the People's Republic of China and the Republic of China both claim to be the only legitimate government of all China.

Bear in mind that allied supply has to be turned off hub-by-hub – for Britain to completely deny allied supply in Dover, for example, supply needs to be turned off at the hubs in London, Portsmouth and the nearby port to the north.

On the left, the US divisions in Dover only have access to hub supply, while on the right, the British divisions there have access to both hub supply and state supply, and so are able to maintain a higher supply state.

On the other hand, doubling the division size does not make the divisions two times more resistant to actual damage, since the organization does not scale up. Damage is two times more frequently dealt to organization instead of HP (which is additive), and defense is often easy to stack up for land units anyways. Having small divisions is additionally more versatile due to the sheer number of divisions, allowing one to run encirclements and cover up extending lines when needed; however this also takes up commanding official capabilities. Small divisions also allow more support weaponry companies to be used, many of which are more economical in their stats contribution per equipment than line companies; on the other hand, they increase the cost of non-weapon support companies, since more of them are needed to achieve the same percentage bonus.

On the surface they seem to be the weakest paths excluding the puppet paths as they necessitate a civil war which significantly slows you down before the actual WW2. Indeed, the democratic PSL path is inferior to Sanation Poland for the most part, and the ability to buy colonies is from the Allies is almost never relevant, since Africa in game is a desolate wasteland with few resources and industry. However, the independent Communist path has the focus "Support Colonial Workers' Strike", which gives you +0.15 extra daily compliance. For this reason alone this path, in some sense, is the strongest path in the whole game; since as a Communist government you will have access to the "Liberated Workers" occupation law, which when coupled with the daily compliance, means that you will have full access to every region's industry and resources within a year of occupying its territory, akin to coring them, only without the extra manpower. This also mean you can usually pop out a collaboration government within a year of occupation, making peace deals very favourable to you; and you can always milk your collaboration puppet of their manpower before re-annexing them. The problem is that this is also likely the hardest path to play in the game, since you have to fight a civil war and there is no free land to be given in the tree except for Liberia, so you will have to fight for every piece of land you own. Additionally you will have few allies, as this path antagonises the Soviet Union and essentially everyone around you. Depending on luck, you might still be able to join the Comintern, but it is not rare for the USSR to have "strategic reasons not to invite you to their faction."

Once a civil war breaks out, the country breaks into two separate entities. How it divides varies for non-scripted civil wars; the amount of land given to a side depends on the popular support for the ideology leading it. For this reason, for effective coups, it is recommended that the "Stage a coup" action is coupled with the "Boost party popularity", as increasing the support for an ideology higher will also increase the size of the break-away state. The two sides, the loyalists and the rebels, immediately enter a state of war with each other, fighting to unite the country under their flag. Once started, a civil war will act as a normal war with victory points eventually leading to capitulation as they fall. The only difference being that there are no occupation laws for occupied territory owned by the other side.

Once a country has lost owned territory above a certain threshold that depends on its war support, it will capitulate. All divisions they own in their ⟦0⟧ or occupied territory will be disbanded and their ⟦1⟧ territory will be instantly occupied by the aggressor, but they carry on as a government-in-exile and keep control of their colonies (non-core provinces) - for example, the Netherlands keeps control of the Dutch East Indies. Partisans in occupied territory will continue to be a problem as long as the country's fellow faction members carry on the war - after all, they can still hope for liberation.

Once a country has upgraded its agency at least 3⟦0⟧ times, is independent or a ⟦1⟧ (⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧), and is a part of a ⟦6⟧, it can choose to invest ⟦7⟧⟦8⟧ to become its faction's Spy Master. Once a focus has started, the player can manually stop it, unless explicitly prohibited. If stopped, a maximum of 10 days of focus progress is saved. If, due to circumstances, the focus has been invalidated, the political power already spent are lost. As such, it is recommended to check all requirements and conditions regarding a focus to assess if/how they may be affected within its completion time-frame.

Once a paradrop executes, the division may suffer losses if its paradrop is disrupted. These losses can occur even when the target province is empty, i.e., when it does not have an enemy division in it. Based on repeated tests of the same drop (i.e., the same order form the same save file), such losses do not seem to be dependent on air superiority (i.e., it happens even when at 100% air superiority), but ⟦14⟧ can contribute to how much a division is disrupted.⟦15⟧ Such losses also seem to occur much more frequently when the drop is at higher latitudes (e.g., in Norway or Northern China), or into coastal provinces.
