While seemingly the weakest warlord, Sinkiang has one key advantage of not being non-aligned as with the other warlords. This allows justification of war regardless of world tension and makes it possible to join Comintern at start. Since the USSR has no interest whatsoever to any Chinese territory, you can justify on other warlords and have the USSR win the wars for you, and claim the land for free. One may also beg for the equipment desperately needed, though the Soviet Union tends to have a large equipment deficit, so you may have to resort for guns from elsewhere, such as Germany after the Anchluss.

While slowly becoming fascist, make sure to construct civil and military factories as well as naval dockyards, Sweden has a decent navy but if playing the long game, a much stronger navy is a must, in particular if participating in the 2nd World War. You should also not disband your current fleets, but should station them it in Malmö (the southern tip of Sweden just east of Copenhagen), it can be given an exercise order but will most likely deplete your fuel stockpile unless you find enough people to buy oil from. As for military you can make do with 20 width infantry with support engineers, recon, artillery, anti-air, and anti-tank - not a particularly good combination but a decent "jack of all trades", but you should make sure you have at least 12 by the time you declare war on Denmark, however keep training more!

While some vessels in service are older models, Italy has several modern battleships, cruisers, destroyers, and submarines under construction, notably two 1936 ⟦0⟧-class and two ⟦1⟧-class battleships, many of which are nearing completion.
While somewhat soggy, the Swamp Fox knows his way around Swamps and Marshes.

While still on Steam right click the Hearts of Iron IV game, select Properties, click on the LOCAL FILES tab, then click on the VERIFY INTEGRITY OF GAME FILES button. This will validate the game files just installed. An "All files successfully validated" message should be seen.

While the ⟦0⟧ AI seems to slightly favor letting you break away cleanly, sometimes it still takes the option for a War goal. If relations are low, it seems to be about even odds if they'll actually use this War goal on you. If you have higher relations they typically will not declare war. We really don't want them to declare war because it can mess up your Naval invasion later.

While the ⟦0⟧ does not have hard World Tension thresholds for its national focuses, Two Ocean Navy Act and Selective Training Act require higher support in Congress if World Tension is less than 50%. It can also struggle to get the War support it needs for The Giant Wakes if World Tension is kept low.

While the AI won’t do this, if you want allies not to be involved on a particular front, it’s possible to toggle off supply for allies on a hub-by-hub basis. To toggle supply for allies off (or back on) for a particular hub, click on the hub, and then select the blue flag to the left and above the supply hub symbol (see examples below).

While the civil war is ongoing, the Confederacy possesses the ability to establish collaborationist governments in fully controlled non-core US states to gain cores on them. When the Confederacy establishes a collaborationist state government, it will gain a core on that state, and the United States will lose its core on that state alongside all congress seats from that state. This can be done on all starting core states of the United States.

While the close-knit crews of [From.GetAdjective] ships offer few avenues of infiltration, the support staff back home is another matter. Getting someone on the inside would give us valuable information as well as the opportunity to support more difficult operations later.

While the current strategy listed here does this with historical AI focuses, it is possible to reroll for a good non-historical run where the UK decolonizes (or even better, disbands the Allies by joining the Axis or Comintern). If the following strategy doesn't work for you, try that.

While the exact focuses the player can take and the exact order these focuses are taken may vary from player to player, it is recommended to have completed as many of the Continue the Zuiderzee Works, War on Pacifism, Appoint New Supreme Commander, and Lessons from the Low Countries focuses as practical by the time the war begins, or as shortly after the war begins as possible.

While the exact military strategy used by the player to gain this achievement is left up to the player's own discretion, use of Line Artillery in Infantry divisions is recommended to adjust for the relatively high industry and low manpower of the Benelux. Additionally, while any land doctrine may be employed, given that the Lessons from the Low Countries national spirit provides 10% extra max entrenchment, and that the player will almost always have a Field Marshal with Defensive Doctrine in Henri Winkelman, it is more advantageous than usual to employ the Grand Battleplan doctrine for the additional entrenchment speed it provides (although this is by no means obligatory). Support Anti-Tank and Support Anti-Air are also highly recommended inclusions in the player's Infantry divisions.

While the flag and the value arguments are self-explanatory, ⟦0⟧ checks how many days it was ⟦1⟧ (Not how many are remaining), while the ⟦2⟧ checks the date at which the flag is set. Every argument aside from the ⟦3⟧ one is optional, just assumed to be always true if not set. This trigger will still always fail if the flag was never set or if it was cleared.

While the limit of deployed anti-tank guns has likely been reached, a new generation of tanks will carry more advanced weaponry, which is able to pierce any current level of protection at long range.

While the player is building up their industry and military they should also keep an eye on what ⟦0⟧ is up to as this strategy relies on waiting for Japan to attack China and then waiting until Japan is firmly into China before betraying them as a well-timed betrayal can potentially allow Manchukuo to fell both countries in one fell swoop. One should ideally wait until Japan has forced China to around 50% surrender progress, as by that point, Japan's forces will be deep in Central China, far away from Manchukuo, and betraying them at that point could allow Manchukuo to quickly conquer the Western parts of China before Japan is able to react properly, which could cause many Japanese divisions to end up caught and trapped between the Manchurian and Chinese forces and destroyed.

While the territory does start as a minor nation, control of Singapore could be vital for dominance in the Asia-Pacific region due to its highly strategic location in addition to being a choke point, something that eventually becomes apparent once ⟦0⟧ expands as part of their plans for a Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere (GEAPS).

While the US's democratic path is powerful, due to it's slow start usually requiring the player to, at the earliest, wait until the Panay Incident, the player can get to war much faster if it opts to abandon Democracy and embrace an alternate idea - in this case, Communism. Siding with Stalin and/or Mao is far more interesting of a game, and in the case of Mao, can hilariously derail the Sino-Japanese war by forcing the nationalists and Japanese to adjust to a third faction entering if one takes "Secure China".
While these aren't scopes, not changing where the effects are run or triggers are checked, they still function as blocks of code that can be used within any trigger and/or effect.
While this has identical effects regardless of whether the country is independent or is a subject, this doesn't access the ⟦0⟧ scope for an independent country.

While this is all taking place, it is also worth keeping an eye on what Japan is up to in terms of National Focuses. One branch of their National Focus tree, specifically ⟦0⟧ and all Focuses after it, allows Japan to improve the industrial base of Manchukuo, so it might just be wise to stay loyal and obedient until Japan has managed to complete all focuses in The Manchurian Project branch as Manchukuo has nothing but benefits to gain from this.

While this is true for most aspects of modding, checking the error log has never been more critical than when modding MIOs: The simple fact that most errors impact the start of a game, are unfixable once it is running and that MIOs affect the game in the long run make it simple to waste a lot of time only to have to reset after all.

While this may seem like you will not finish the latter before the ⟦0⟧ finishes, the game will prioritize the player's focus as long as it completes on the same day (and both of the latter focuses will bypass the Terror Center). Additionally, if we take the focus that bypasses the aforementioned Center focus before, Stalin will merely speed up his focuses, whereas if we let it play out but not finish, he'll be on the same track but we'll be closer. While it might seem ideal to purge army officers because of how many you have, if you need to lower paranoia, focus on purging the navy - while you have more generals, the navy is not as important to the Soviet Union as it is to the British or Japanese. Generate new admirals as needed, and also forge production reports if you don't have the option to purge an admiral. Only purge officers if you have no other choice.

While this national reconstruction project is ongoing, one should also begin to look abroad and take stock of the situation. Depending on how long the reconquest and reunification of China took, the game will likely now be in the early 1940s, and World War II likely well underway. This gives Qing China many possible avenues of action (once they are sufficiently prepared).
While waiting for the ⟦0⟧ justification get a chief of army so you can build army XP and get Ideological Loyalty for the +500 manpower per week. Your manpower is too small without this.

While weakened, if properly played, Vichy France is still capable of digging itself out of this morass and then either joining the Axis as an equal to Germany after asking them to end the occupation, defecting to the Allies and uniting with Free France, or taking a third option and regaining their honor by defeating Germany by themselves.

While winter attrition can be reduced by appointing the armies to a commander with a ⟦0⟧ trait, there is no corresponding trait to reduce heat attrition. Commanders gain the ⟦1⟧ trait by fighting for a longer time in cold weather. ⟦2⟧ has a unique focus Desert Equipment reducing heat attrition.

While you can go for the traditional historical path, going Democratic is arguably a more interesting option - not only does this let the European powers focus on their home front, it also allows you to bring the western colonies in Asia closer to self rule - the US can still join the allies once tension gets high enough.

While you can liberate the Philippines through a focus, one should hold off until the Philippines flips to communism - do this through the "Socialist Education" decision. After they flip, go ahead and liberate them.

While you do have a weak army, they have a much weaker army and should capitulate fairly easily. During the peace conference, puppet them and liberate Samoa as a puppet as well. With the help of your puppets, declare on the Dutch East Indies. They'll call in their overlords, the Netherlands, but you just need to capitulate the Dutch East Indies and the Netherlands should just back off.

While you wait to turn fascist, use your one civilian factory to build some more civs, and take your industrial focuses to get some free civilian and military factories, which will be very valuable, since Liberia has next-to-none starting factories. Once you finish turning fascist, you can now progress down the rest of your political focuses to get that extra recruitable population. Also, at this point you should have researched Basic Machine Tools, Dispersed/Concentrated Industry, Construction One, as well as some Electronics techs to boost research speed and maybe some Infantry techs to boost soft attack. Artillery is highly recommended but probably not feasible given Liberia's limited research slots- so is Close Air Support. Try to fit these in if you can. Your political power, should also be spent first on getting to war economy for 150 political power, then take some Improved Worker Conditions, Anti-Democratic/Communist Raids to get your stability up, and then if you have enough political power, a Captain of Industry. At this point, it should be around late 1938, to mid 1939, and here you can make a decision. Either you can join the Axis and use your limited army to quickly grab some Allied land- or you can build up your army and industry, wait for the Allies to pull their troops out of Africa, and ⟦0⟧ strike. Both are feasible, but this guide will focus on you waiting. But if you want to quickly attack, go ahead- it will mostly be a game of cat-and-mouse for you, since your units will melt when faced with any Allied troops, so your main focus will be shifting your units around to pin down as much enemy troops as you can as you wait for Germany and Italy to come to your rescue.

While you'll have removed the economic debuffs by the time you complete Re-Integration, you can still take Federal Housing Act for additional building slots if you haven't flipped to communism (you'll be able to bypass Fair Labor Standards Act thanks to the focuses you can access after Union Representation Act).

While you're taking down the USA, prepare for war with France. If world tension is over 25% then France will guarantee most nations that you justify on. Justify on the Netherlands, who France will guarantee. Once ready, naval invade the Netherlands. Attack the Dutch East Indies too so you can annex them in the peace deal. Do not call your dominions into the war. Rush the Dutch VPs and they'll go down easily. The moment France joins the war, begin justifying on Belgium. You're fascist, so your time taken to justify will be ⟦0⟧ faster while you're at war with a major (France), make use of it. Declare on Belgium, rush its VPs, then rush on Paris to bring France down. Before France falls, start one last justification on a strategic nation like Turkey or Iraq.

While you're working on the justification, start going down the Nationalist Ethos side of the political focus tree. This will grant you a 7% Recruitable Population, something that is highly covered and useful for small nations as it boosts your manpower.
Whilst the achievement toolbox doesn't mention it, but you need the Turkish territories in Balkans for it to trigger.

Whilst the coups are underway/preparing take all focuses up to United, We Shall Prevail! do not take The Unification of the Balkans. After each individual coup launches, you can join the civil wars on the communist side and invite Yugoslavia to the wars.

Why? First of all, the time it takes to complete the latter focus is HUGE. It takes 210 days just to get to the point where you finally are able to target the Warlords or the Communists, and it takes a further 70 days just to target each of them, respectively. What this means is that just by declaring war (not conquering yet) at them takes almost an entire year, this, combined with the fact that you'd likely want to at least complete the first 2 focuses to gain the 3rd research slot, leaves you only with 1~2 months to stomp out all other political entities before Japan attacks you. Or, if you forsake the 3rd research slot (which is desperately needed given the technological inferiority compared to Japanese), you still only have around half a year to stomp them out.

For bomber strikes, a strategic bomber wing is required, while for ⟦2⟧ strikes, an MRBM or ICBM is required. The bombers are launched from Air Bases while the missiles are launched from Rocket Sites or from a ⟦3⟧ deployed from a Naval base. Once a nation has researched and developed all three delivery methods (bombers, terrestrial missiles and submarine missiles), they will have access to the full Nuclear trifecta.

With ⟦0⟧, the Raj has a sprawling focus tree that can be very powerful, but is also full of "trap" options that appear beneficial on paper but end up being detrimental in practice. Examples of these "trap" options include Swadeshi Movement (whose long completion time, increased resistance target, and lack of meaningful unlocks end up making the one ⟦1⟧ and pitiful autonomy increase it provides not worth it), Princely States Policy (whose ⟦2⟧ do not actually provide any meaningful benefits after accounting for the misleading way the game handles ⟦3⟧), and Defense Of India Act (which does not provide any real benefits over sticking to ⟦4⟧ at peace-time and ⟦5⟧ at wartime even if it can be taken early thanks to the Axis powers generating a lot of early World Tension). It can also be very easy to inadvertently sabotage Raj's build by taking certain focuses too early, e.g., taking Agricultural Cooperatives before it gives at least 2 ⟦6⟧ or taking military factory focuses too early and therefore wasting their size increase effects for key military industrial organizations on smaller sizes that would require fewer funds to increase normally, thus unnecessarily delaying the incredibly powerful The Ordnance Factories Board. It is therefore important to prioritize: focus on economy- and research-related focuses early, pivot to military factory-related focuses afterwards, and then focus on picking up the numerous stats bonuses that Raj has in their new focus tree, including from Lions of the Great War, Model After Soviet Union, Specialized Dietary Requirement, Inclusive Nationalism, and South East Asia Command (the bonuses of which are contained in an event that fires immediately after its completion). Special attention should also be paid to For the People, By the People, as its research bonuses can be used to get earlier access to critical infantry weapon technologies, usually either ⟦7⟧ or ⟦8⟧ depending on who else is rushing those technologies on the Allies. Acquiring ⟦9⟧ status and, eventually, freedom is still helpful and can be done with the same convoy lend-lease tricks as without the DLC, but is not as vital to get done as early as possible as it is without the DLC. Once all stat bonuses have been acquired, it is likely a good idea to pick up as many focuses that will prevent the spread of famine. The Bengal Famine is especially devastating with ⟦10⟧, and reaching 100% famine spread prevention as early as possible is vital to making sure it only lasts 6-10 months instead of the years that it can otherwise last. Remember to have ⟦11⟧ researched before the famine starts to be able to immediately use the decision unlocked by Quinine.

With 1.9 alongside La Resistance, the Sino-Japanese War can easily turn into a meat grinder for Japan. Be sure to complete Develop Chinese Resources focus first before allowing the collaboration government to form or you will lose out on its bonuses. You can form the Collaboration Government with either Nationalist China or Communist China. Using Communist China as collaboration government might be a preferable option given their better national spirits and conscription laws but you will need more garrison during the time you are completing the focus as the compliance will only form in their starting area. Keep in mind that just like normal puppets, collaboration government will not give you access to their docks and the collaboration puppet will immediately form over all their core territory you possess during their formation which including Dalian, East Hebei, and Taiwan.

With 6 carriers, the carrier overstacking penalty prevents -100399500% of all carrier wings from targeting enemy ships, rounded down. For this penalty, the first four carriers count as having only 1 air wing each. The 5th carrier counts as having 2 air wings and the 6th carrier counts as having 3 air wings. This gives a total of 9 carrier air wings. -100399500% of 9 is 9035964 air wings, and which rounds down to 9035964 air wings that can target enemy ships. These wings are counted from those based on the first carrier in the list going downward. This means that the naval bombers on the first 5 carriers will operate as normal, while the naval bombers and CAS on carrier number 6 will not launch attacks at enemy ships, but they will still take off and be vulnerable to enemy fighters. The carrier fighters on carriers number 5 and 6 are unaffected by the penalty, and so will fly and can target enemy aircraft regardless.

With historical AI disabled, the fastest way is to invade Germany first. Head north, take the cities and annex Germany. This will get you two provinces closer. Next, invade France. Just heading into the Maginot Line is going to be a suicide mission, so head through Belgium (Schlieffen 2: Electric Boogaloo) and Britain is almost certainly going to guarantee France or Belgium, so you can also bring down Britain with them. And Italy might just join the Axis to bog you down, so hoping that the Austro-Hungarian military has been built up significantly, you can do a mass invasion of Western Europe. Getting to Paris will bring down the French, and they will surrender after about half of the country is occupied. Then go around Switzerland to Italy's western border and attack. This will be a surprise attack for the Italians, so rush down the peninsula and do a naval invasion of Palestine and Lebanon. Go down to Egypt, seize the Suez Canal (you should also have seized Malta and Cyprus by now) and march into Algeria. Once you have Algiers, navally invade Gibraltar. This will make supply lines to the British Raj and the Antipodes longer and costlier, weakening the eastern half of the British Empire. Then put all your troops on the north coast of France and navally invade England. When the treaties come, take as much land as possible and what you also need for the achievement. As soon as you hold all the provinces necessary, you can get the achievement.

With the right designs, these bonuses can help massively reduce the ⟦0⟧ cost of producing expensive equipment, like heavy tanks with heavy cannons or aircraft with self-sealing fuel tanks. If a country has additional equipment conversion speed bonuses from elsewhere, making equipment in two steps can even be outright cheaper.

With the Royal Titles restored, and the Kaiserin on the throne, you now have the Benelux, Italy, and Switzerland left to conquer before you can form the HRE. While you can manually justify a war goal on Italy (as a non-aligned nation, tension will be high enough, and Italy will have caused world tension), it is much easier to guarantee the independence of either Greece or Yugoslavia, and have them call you in when Italy inevitably declares war on one of them (naval invasions on the Italian coastal cities in combination with a few collaboration governments should do the trick). Afterwards, defeat Italy, take the northern Italian territories (Piedmont (158), Lombardy (159), South Tyrol (39), Veneto (160), Emilia Romagna (161), Tuscany (162) and Istria (736)) required, and leave the Allies (feel free to take See to the Eastern Front and Danzig for Guarantee to return Memel to your borders and have East Prussia connected at this point; you can later form a faction with Poland if you wish, who likely are still non-aligned and are inclined to join a faction with you). Garrison troops on the UK's victory points, justify on the Benelux countries or Switzerland (due to how high world Tension is, if the UK is controlled by an AI, they will guarantee them), and when the war is declared, the British will join, which will cause them to come close to capitulating, if not instantly capitulating. If Man the Guns is installed, there's a very good chance that the Netherlands has joined the Allies by this point, so you could justify on either Belgium or Luxembourg and also get the Dutch in the peace deal. If playing with Man the Guns, it's recommended that one do this sooner rather than later, as there is a chance that if the British have not taken their political focuses, they will take a Change in Course and go Fascist/Communist (if they take the former, they'll join the Japanese on historical; if they go the latter, they'll join the USSR). Take whatever you want during the peace deal (while you cannot get territory from Australia, Canada, New Zealand, or South Africa unless you occupied them, fought them directly, or dropped one bomb on them through strategic bombing, you can satellite British Malaya and the Raj; if you do wish to go after the British dominions, however, you should have territory to stage naval invasions from thanks to the French lands of Madagascar (543), St. Pierre and Miquelon (730), and New Caledonia (635), and compared to the Royal Navy, the colonial navies are relatively weak), and then focus on taking down the remaining Benelux countries and Switzerland - the latter can be defeated easily if you use a trap, tricking them into coming onto territory you control (outside of the mountains), and then rushing their victory points. Afterwards, take the decision and restore the HRE. If you took Danzig for Guarantee and See to the Eastern Front, congratulate yourself on restoring not just the HRE, but Prussia to German hands.

Within their names, variables can have any word character, i.e. the 26 English letters (Either lowercase or uppercase), underscores, and the decimal digits from 0 to 9. However, a variable name cannot ⟦0⟧ with a decimal digit, so a name like ⟦1⟧ is invalid. This requirement common in many programming languages, and is implemented here for the same reason that the ⟦2⟧ prefix exists: so that the parser can determine what syntactic type a token will be from the first (few) characters, and therefore doesn't have to worry about backtracking as much. In addition, it is recommended to avoid any names by variables that are already used for something else. For example, naming a variable ⟦3⟧ can prevent any subsequent usage of the ⟦4⟧ within the internal code. A common naming convention to avoid overlap is to add a prefix signifying where it's used, such as the country's tag (⟦5⟧) or the name of the mechanic (Usually shortened like ⟦6⟧).

Rushing to complete Quit India Movement and Two-Nation Theory may seem wasteful, but they stop and slowly reverse the passive autonomy decline Raj experiences from the start of the game, which can allow them to take more investment focuses later without jeopardizing their position. The choice of what to use Vickers-Berthier Gun on can also be important, with ⟦2⟧ usually being such a good candidate that Raj should often rush to try to get that technology as early as possible with the help of that focus. Achieving ⟦10⟧ status early is also important to be able to complete Indian Gentlemen Officers, which, together with ⟦11⟧, will allow Raj to fix their shortage of generals with newly recruited ones who are often better than the ones with which it starts.

You must have the highest war score of all participants. It may be easier to annex a single state, release it, justify a second war against the Soviets, and capitulate them alone.

You need either a limited success, success, or critical success for the raid to count. The sole exception for this is the Austrian Reichstags Raid. It will award the achievement even if the raid results in a failure (this is likely an oversight).

You need to continue working the Balkans. This will most likely drain your Political Power quite a lot, so prepare for a fairly long journey. The key is to invite ⟦0⟧ (which you will not long after conquer/puppet) but only invite ⟦1⟧ in the end ( Germany is not an option) so they won't get anything.

You need to declare war on China and Japan before 1940. Capitulation on the other hand has no time limit. The requirement to "capitulated" means you must achieve the highest score in the war against China and the highest score in the war against Japan.
You need to either annex all USA core states, or puppet the USA and let it have all core states.

You need to go down the "Election Overturned" Hispanic road. After that, complete the rest of the Hispanic focuses and take decisions with Hispanic countries with the Hispanic Overtures focus. I recommend improving relations and using a diplomatic pressure agent. After completing the "War of Independence", you need to hold the USA for a year to get the white peace event. ⟦0⟧

You need to move your fleet into the Black Sea before Turkey remilitarises the Bosphorus Strait. You can increase its range by basing it in Cyprus. Go down the Empower the Workers path towards Join Comintern. Justify a wargoal on ⟦0⟧ and attack from the ⟦1⟧. Turkey will guard Istanbul, but leave Erdine undefended. Call them into the war and naval invade ⟦2⟧ ⟦3⟧. The achievement only requires control of the state, so it can be gained while at war.
You no longer require French Somaliland for the Chilean empire achivement
You now control ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧ and England. This allows you to reform the ⟦3⟧ and, more importantly, the far more powerful North Sea Empire, giving you loads of ⟦4⟧ and factories.
You now have a couple of options for what to do next.

You now have a very strong industrial and manpower base in order to take down ⟦0⟧. You probably already have more troops than they do, so go ahead and justify a war goal on them. Set your cruiser and 2 submarines to Patrol in the Lower Baltic Sea, and set up naval invasions from your southern ports to take their ports. As you are getting the justification, you should aim to have 40 divisions in the field and trained with Support Anti-Air added as soon as reasonably possible. This is for a contingency.
You now have nine of thirteen counties.

You now have to take 5 70-day focuses (Confirm the Fueros, Settle the Succession Question, Dios, Patria y Rey!, Restore the Empire, Claim the French Throne) to get a casus belli against France. (Carlist Spain is non-aligned and it requires 50% world tension to justify wars).
You now only need >25% more pressure than Pakistan/Bangladesh to win a princely state
You only need around 180 Towed Artillery at the most, so you can grab some trucks and trains later on if you feel you're set on guns and artillery.
You only need to have had more than 30% surrender progress after 1941.06.22 once, and not necessarily when at war with the required countries.

You only need to occupy the state. Turn fascist and justify on ⟦0⟧. Build ~10 submarines and declare war. Capture a port in Greenland and then invade ⟦1⟧. Note that you ⟦2⟧ be in a faction with countries outside South America.

You only need to occupy the states, not own them. Switch to communist and get as many Balkan countries as possible in your faction. The country will flip above 60% communist support ( ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ are particularly important to get on your side). Any Balkan country in your faction can be annexed through the The Unification of the Balkans focus. Once you have established the Federation, attack whoever still controls land in the Balkans and capitulate ⟦2⟧. ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧ needs to be in a faction when they capitulate to satisfy the "at war" and "has capitulated" requirements. Otherwise when they capitulate, they are no longer at war and the achievement doesn't fire.

You should also do the usual starting actions, pick techs, arrange army, ideally strip them of weapons and start training to regular a select few that will go as volunteers in ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ - also start training filler troops - 3 Cavalry template - and give them weapons gradually then deploy them at 20%, as you need to save weapons; also consider disbanding the tank division - not the template.

You should be able to gain independence before the end of the war, through war contribution and the autonomy focus. You need a decent war score because you gained cores on eastern Germany, you need your old cores and the eastern German provinces to get the achievement.

You should be able to take East Prussia with relative ease (it's not uncommon for the AI to have it practically empty at that point) and to push back on Germany, once their initial assault is stopped and you have East Prussia.

You should be strong enough to capitulate ⟦0⟧ through manpower alone, once the war ends take Lappland for yourself. You can now continue down to Ostland to get the achievement as Germany will accept your request to join the Axis since you're not at war anymore.

You should choose for your starting focus "Transfer the New Zealand division" and continue down the naval path until you have dockyards. Then set your 2 cruisers to do exercises, and the dockyards can repair them. Once that is done, rush down the "Maori affairs"(?) side of the political tree, taking the Maori volunteers route at the split at the bottom, and skipping the original Maori Affairs Act for now. Then rush down the political side that has you go independent, but do not take the final focus yet, or you will leave the allies, and be left on your own against Japan. Then complete the naval tree, choosing submarines over destroyers, and skipping light cruiser effort.

You should have ~24 divisions in the field by the time you take Demand Iraqi Territory and Demand Afghan Territory (they tend to accept; they are more likely to accept if you have a significantly larger army and they are under 50% war support.) At some point, you'll need to switch to Limited Conscription (possibly by taking the Absolute Monarchy focus). Switch straight to Service by Requirement as soon as the game allows (this will be when you are at war with a sufficiently large enemy) - manpower is your major handicap; until you gain some new cores, you can't field much more than ~30 divisions in with Limited Conscription, you are not allowed to switch to higher conscription laws in peacetime because you're non-aligned, and you have to stay non-aligned to be eligible for this branch of the focus tree. Build a supply depot in the northernmost province of West Azerbaijan (the one adjacent to Van and Yerevan) and another in the easternmost province of Herat.
You should have 30-ish strong divisions along your western border and another 30-ish along the border with East Prussia, in addition to 24 in Czechoslovakia.

You should have almost all, if not all of your soldiers, back by now, since they should be either exiled from your recently decolonized lands or because you brought them back. Once Concede to the Trade Unions is completed, begin

You should have enough troops to scare ⟦0⟧ into quick submission. There are many guides on how to exploit the civil war, but in short, if you want to help your brothers, try to encircle the nationalist and eliminate them, try to head north, otherwise, just go somewhere cosy and enjoy the static warfare and seemingly limitless experience (though note that the Italian and German planes might ruin your vacation).

You should have five full armies now - four using puppeted manpower (either Brazilian or Argentinian) and one made up of mountaineers with SPGs. Ideally you use your own manpower for this last army, but if you're low, just use Brazil's manpower, as they will never run out. ⟦0⟧

You will want to invade Greece as they are your weakest neighbor so turn Fascist or Communist and justify upon them (fascism is advised as the Axis are bordering you and are potentially more useful allies and the manpower gained from militarism is a good buff). Do not puppet Greece as Italy can get a war goal on them and it would take a large naval buildup to challenge the Italian Navy not to mention that Italy would call in Germany providing they are both Fascist and Germany would be very difficult to hold off. If the world tension is low enough or ww2 has started, justify on Turkey. You should navally invade as the Bosporus straits are difficult to cross. After this, you could invade Yugoslavia although you may want to be quick because they tend to join the Axis or Allies. You will want to take the "Form Collaboration Government" decision as soon as they capitulate, either via event or decision. This is insurance since it protects your winnings - you now own the US states indirectly, and don't have to pay for them in the peace deal.

You'll end up either in your own faction or as part of the Allies (if you complete "A Habsburg Alliance" after the beginning of the war, you'll leave the Allies and start your own faction.) Either way, you'll likely have at least one Baltic state fighting alongside you before long. Don't count on any help from Western Europe - they'll happily sit and watch, or, at best, send a navy to the Baltic. You can start working on "Between The Seas" focuses while you're fighting, to add more allies to your faction (though many of them will be reluctant.)

You'll likely need to make a few runs to hit on a favorable arrangement of factions. The optimal scenario is one where ⟦0⟧ stays out of factions till after your civil war, and where the ⟦1⟧ either goes solo (uncommon) or ends up in a weak faction (typically because the UK goes fascist).

You'll need to form a faction in order to get the Scandinavian nations into it and to ultimately annex them, but that doesn't invalidate the achievement requirements as you only mustn't JOIN a faction. Creating a faction yourself is allowed as of patch 1.13.3.

You'll need to immediately turn your attention towards mainland Europe. Join all wars that the ⟦0⟧ is in (if you aren't already) and retake France, Italy, and the Balkans. Afterwards, you'll need to capitulate the Soviets. All the while, you will have to leave a beefy naval garrison in place on the Home Islands (at minimum one full army) because the ⟦1⟧ will constantly naval invade it.

You're going to be starved for Political Power for a while. I recommend getting the Silent Workhorse and Nationalist Lutheran Priest with your first free political power. Immediately after that, take the Entice the Masses (Balance of Power), Anti-Democratic Raids, and Anti-Communist Raids decisions in order to stabilize your Public Trust. You'll need to run these raids multiple times most likely. Alternatively (in part), you can just Ban Democratic Parties instead as soon as they drop under 20%.

Your best bet is probably to play non-historical and restart until Germany goes for its civil war. Forming ⟦0⟧ is critical before attacking Germany, since you need more cores to build up a large enough army. If you want to make sure that ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧ or the ⟦3⟧ do not attack you, you could keep them at historical focuses. It could, however be beneficial to get a defensive war with ⟦4⟧ when it is time to expand.

Your civilian factory count should even rival the ⟦0⟧ at this point; switch to ⟦1⟧ and just spam out military factories in all of your cores with the best infrastructure. Cut down your army to ~108 divisions and change them all to use a 12-width Infantry template with Heavy Weapons Company regimental support and Support Engineers, Support Artillery, and Support Anti-Air for division support companies at minimum (you can also add in anything else you'd like over time as equipment allows). Set 96 divisions on your border with the ⟦2⟧ and keep 12 back to use to defend against naval invasions. Obviously, you'll be very deep in equipment shortages, but just keep chipping away at them and they should resolve by the time you are attacked in late 1939. Make sure to train your troops before then, too.

Your main aim as the Raj in historical multiplayer is to defend against ⟦0⟧ for as long as possible. How this is best done depends on the game's rules, active DLCs, and how ⟦1⟧ acts in their war against ⟦2⟧. A ⟦3⟧ that blazes through ⟦4⟧ to conquer it quickly will have access to more ⟦5⟧ and ⟦6⟧ for longer but will tend to have less experienced generals due to the lack of ⟦7⟧ opportunities, while a ⟦8⟧ that takes their time will tend to have far more powerful generals and field marshals from ⟦9⟧, and therefore far better stats on their units, at the cost of delaying their access to the rather substantial Chinese industrial base. Time is also usually on the Allies' side, so the longer it takes for ⟦10⟧ to declare war, the easier it should be to deal with them once they have.

Your main enemy in the very early game is Guangxi Clique, not only having basically most of the resources of all of China, but also has a robust industry. As such, this early strike would prevent this warlord nation from building a larger army. Even with the speed of the completion of this focus, they will barely have enough divisions to cover the entire border. This is where China's larger and advanced military comes to play. Use the air force to gain the advantage on single tile battles, use the cavalry and the 6-battalion units to break and exploit lines and use the regular infantry to pin Guangxi Clique's army.

Your objective is to encircle as many ⟦0⟧ divisions as possible, and defend Karachi against naval invasions. When your 5 queued divisions reach the minimum training requirement, force deploy them near a weak part of the front line and use them as an offensive force to get encirclements. If the AI frontline order sent your mountaineer divisions to the south, swap them to the northern mountains to make the most of their attack and movement bonuses in mountain terrain. Once you have advanced to Delhi and encircled enough divisions for there to be multiple gaps in the enemy’s frontline, start snaking for valuable victory points such as Bombay, Nagpur, Lucknow, and Calcutta. If you are able to reach these cities before the ceasefire timer runs out, the ⟦1⟧ will capitulate, and make your future attack much easier. (If you are really lucky and/or sneaky, you can even manage to capitulate British Burma - the key is to seize Rangoon - but you won't get to keep it after the ceasefire, so, you don't need to try hard. Just put troops on the border and keep Burma contained.) The UK will keep running naval invasions nonstop, targeting Karachi, Bombay, and Calcutta/Dacca. Keep forces on fallback lines in all three places.

Your ships should be technologically ahead enough that with a full aircraft complement you can take on navies that out-number you 2 to 1 with minimal casualties.
